Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

flexyBayes 0.18.1

  • On Windows, a brms fit that fails no longer blames a working C++ toolchain.
  • Messages about unrecognised engine settings and fb_engine() options quote the names the same way on every operating system.

flexyBayes 0.18.0

For users of 0.10.0

0.10.0 was the last public release. These changes can stop an existing script or change its results. Each is described in full under its release below.

  • triangulate() and triangulate_genomic() are removed.
  • fb(), fb_inla(), fb_brms(), fb_engine(), fb_from_asreml() and fb_from_brms() are deprecated in favour of flexybayes() and fb_plan(). proceed(), cat_code(), is_fb_cov(), is_fb_engine() and is_fb_approx() are deprecated too. Each still runs and warns with what to call instead.
  • The default prior on each standard deviation is half-normal on both engines and follows the units of the response, so estimates can differ from 0.10.0.
  • INLA fits run on one thread and are fitted three times, keeping the fit with the highest marginal likelihood. The three fits run at the same time, so a fit takes little longer than a single fit. options(flexyBayes.inla_best_of = 1) fits once, and options(flexyBayes.inla_best_of_workers = 1) runs the three one after another, which takes about three times as long.
  • us(f):g and (x | g) fit on brms only, and backend = "auto" sends them there. fa(env, k):gen is refused on both engines.

New since 0.10.0

  • More ASReml syntax: at(), dsum() residuals, AR1 x AR1 fields per trial, predict(classify = ) and predictions for unseen levels. See the vignette Moving from ASReml-R.
  • known_variance for the second stage of a two-stage analysis, and pooled() priors on brms.
  • Every fit records the priors it used (prior_summary()) and how it was run.
  • Refusals carry a reason code, and other packages can register their own with fb_register_refusals().

In this release

  • On INLA fits, a variance component is marked weakly identified when its 95% interval covers 40% or more of its prior’s probability, or is 4.24 or more times its median. Expect more of these warnings than under 0.17.0, mostly on terms with few levels. Under a prior tighter than the default, a component whose interval sits close to its median can be marked as well. The flag can stay silent on a component the data cannot identify, as item 24 of inst/KNOWN_ISSUES.md describes.
  • fa() is still refused. In a simulation test, intervals for the genetic correlation covered the true value 134 and 125 times in 150 for k = 1 and 2, against 136 required. The refusal message gives the details.
  • A field with one AR1 factor names its correlation after that factor, for example rho_t, instead of rho_row.
  • On INLA, summary(fit)$varcomp names the residual prior on each dsum() section.
  • INLA fits run once under R CMD check when cores are limited.
  • The package title is “Bayesian Mixed Models with ASReml Syntax via INLA and brms”.
  • The penalised-selection functions deprecated in 0.16.0, fb_select() and the six beside it, are removed, and glmnet leaves Suggests.

flexyBayes 0.17.0

Changes to fitting

  • Every INLA fit is now run three times, once in the session and twice in fresh R processes, and the fit with the highest log marginal likelihood is returned. Identical one-thread INLA calls in fresh processes can reach different modes, so a single fit is not repeatable across sessions. options(flexyBayes.inla_best_of = 1) fits once, exactly as 0.16.0 did. Other whole numbers set the number of fits. The further fits need callr. A fit takes about three times as long.
  • $extras$reproducibility$best_of records each fit’s log marginal likelihood and mode status, the fit kept, the range of the marginal likelihoods, and how far each standard deviation moved across the fits. print() and summary() add one line when a standard deviation differs by more than 5%.
  • A fit that fails in a separate process stops the call with that process’s message. An option value that is not a whole number of one or more refuses with inla_best_of_invalid.
  • On six trials of a barley series, single fits in eight processes reached four modes. Best of three in four processes reached three, two of them 0.003 apart in log marginal likelihood. Within a process the main-plot standard deviation moved by up to 13.6% and the others by 3.9% or less.
  • The two fresh-process fits of best of three now run at the same time as the fit in the session, so best of three takes little longer than a single fit. On six trials of a barley series a package fit took a median of 29 s, against 64 s with the fits one after another (three fresh processes each). The fit kept does not depend on which fit finishes first: it is the one with the highest log marginal likelihood, the lowest-numbered of equal ones.
  • options(flexyBayes.inla_best_of_workers) sets how many fits run at once, the session fit included. The default is all of them, and 1 runs them one after another as before. Each child runs INLA with the session’s thread plan, "1:1" by default.
  • Before the fits start, the memory one fit needs is estimated from the design-memory preflight and compared with the free memory. When it holds fewer fits than asked for, fewer run at once, down to one after another, and a message says how much memory is free and how much a fit needs. The number of fits is never changed.
  • $extras$reproducibility$best_of now also records each fit’s time in seconds (wall_s), the number of fits run at once (workers) and whether that was more than one (parallel).
  • When fits running at once fail, the call stops with the message of the lowest-numbered failed fit, and the fits still running are ended.
  • Once the last fresh-process fit has finished, the processx supervisor that flexyBayes started for it is ended, so a fit leaves no connection open. A supervisor the session already ran is left running.

New features

  • Model C’s per-trial standard deviations can be partially pooled. fb_prior(sd(group = "TRIAL:VARIETY", by = "TRIAL") ~ pooled(scale = half_normal(scale = 0.5))) pools the genotype-by-trial SDs of diag(TRIAL):VARIETY, and sigma(by = "TRIAL") ~ pooled(scale = ...) pools the residual SDs of dsum(~ units | TRIAL). Either can be used without the other. The log SDs share a normal distribution with an estimated mean and SD. The prior on that SD, scale, has no default, and a pooled() without it is refused.
  • Pooling is fitted on brms only. backend = "inla" refuses with pooled_prior_requires_brms, and backend = "auto" fits on brms and says so in backend_decision() and fb_plan(). Printed fits, summary() and prior_summary() label the fit “per-trial SDs partially pooled” and print each pooling SD’s posterior median.
  • A pooled fit is a different estimator from ASReml’s model C. On the stored 12-trial fixture, T06’s residual variance moved from ASReml’s 0.086 to a posterior median of 0.099 (0.81 ASReml standard errors) and T09’s genotype-by-trial variance from 0.632 to 0.550.
  • Over 20 simulated 12-trial series, the 90% intervals covered the true per-trial SDs at 91% (genotype-by-trial) and 88% (residual), and the true pooling SDs at 80% and 95%. One fit takes about two minutes on two cores.

Factor-analytic covariance

  • fa(env, k):gen is still refused on both engines (factor_analytic_not_repeatable). Fits on INLA did not reproduce ASReml 4.2’s split of the genetic variance into common and specific parts, which ASReml often places at a specific variance of zero.
  • fb_prior() accepts loading(group = "gen") ~ normal(mean, sd), the prior on the loadings of fa(f, k):gen. With none stated the loadings take INLA’s own prior on a copy scaling, normal(mean = 1, sd = 0.316), which is named in the model manifest.
  • ASReml 4.2 reference fits of fa(env, k):gen on agridat::besag.met (all genotypes and the first 30) and agridat::dasilva.maize ship in inst/validation/asreml-4.2/.

Other changes

  • The seven selection functions deprecated in 0.16.0 (fb_select() and the six beside it) still stop with selection_removed and remain exported in this release.

Documentation

  • An INLA fit is not guaranteed to give the same result in a fresh R session, even on one thread. Earlier help pages said it was. The measurements, and a check to run where a conclusion rests on a weakly informed variance, are in ?flexybayes (section INLA threads) and inst/KNOWN_ISSUES.md (item 26).

flexyBayes 0.16.0

Breaking changes

  • Penalised selection is no longer part of flexyBayes. fb_select(), fb_select_path(), fb_select_refit(), fb_select_fold_data(), fb_penalty(), fb_resamples() and fb_decision() remain in this release and stop with the refusal selection_removed. They will be removed in the next one. The vignette A two-stage analysis of a series of trials now shows a penalised regression fitted with glmnet on the design whitened by fb_marginal_cov(), and the vignette Selecting over a candidate block is withdrawn. The options flexyBayes.selection_dense_gb, flexyBayes.selection_grouped_solver and flexyBayes.selection_workers are no longer read, and projpred, grpreg, quadprog and plotly leave Suggests.

    # Before
sel <- fb_select(fit, ~ z1 + z2, penalty = fb_penalty(term(everything()) ~ laplace(scale = 0.3)))
# Now: whiten the design X and response y by the fitted covariance, and
# fit the path with glmnet
U <- chol(as.matrix(fb_marginal_cov(fit)))
glmnet::cv.glmnet(backsolve(U, X, transpose = TRUE),
                  backsolve(U, y, transpose = TRUE), intercept = FALSE)

  • lgm_gate() no longer runs its check for joint shrinkage priors, which no route reached, and the refusal prior_family_unsupported_inla is gone.

  • This renames the correlations of every field whose factors are not called row and col: ar1(ROW):ar1(RANGE) now reports rho_ROW and rho_RANGE, where it reported rho_row and rho_col. For ar1(range):ar1(row), rho_row is now the correlation along row, which was rho_col before, and the correlation along range is rho_range. A field written ar1(row):ar1(col) keeps its names. A fit saved with an earlier version keeps the old names in summary() until it is refitted, and fb_marginal_cov() refuses such a fit by name.

  • On brms, allow_new_levels = TRUE used to pass through to posterior_epred() with brms’s default new-level policy, which resamples the effects of seen levels and leaves out observation noise. It now returns the table above, built from posterior_predict(sample_new_levels = "gaussian").

  • at_field_per_level_parameters_not_fitted and at_field_per_level_hyper_not_representable leave the refusal registry, since both spellings now fit. The nugget-free residual beside a random-side field refuses (ar1_residual_with_random_field), and residual = ~ ar1(t) still refuses.

New features

  • predict(fit, newdata, allow_new_levels = TRUE) predicts trials and localities the fit did not see, on INLA and on brms. Each level the fit did not see is drawn from its fitted variance, and an INLA fit’s AR1 x AR1 field is drawn afresh for a new trial. Levels the fit saw keep their own posterior effects. mean_by = ~ TRIAL gives the mean of each trial’s rows, ~ TRIAL + VARIETY + NRATE each cell mean. The result is a table of predictive means, SDs and intervals, observation noise included, with joint draws in attr(, "draws"), and it repeats under set.seed().

  • On INLA the mean and SD are exact for the posterior draws used. At ASReml 4.2’s REML variances the variance of a trial, cell or locality mean agrees with ASReml’s plug-in value to 2e-15.

  • A structure the new-level draw is not built for (random slopes, splines, known covariances, factor-analytic and unstructured terms, observation weights, a known variance), a new level with no fitted variance (a new level of f in diag(f):g, a new residual section, a plot off the fitted lattice) and a non-Gaussian response are refused by name: predict_new_levels_structure_not_supported, predict_new_levels_no_variance and predict_new_levels_family_not_supported.

  • A series of trials with its own genotype-by-trial variance and its own residual variance in every trial, random = ~ ... + diag(TRIAL):VARIETY with residual = ~ dsum(~ units | TRIAL), now fits on INLA past 15 variance parameters. Above that limit INLA fits it by empirical Bayes (int.strategy = "eb"). The fixed and random effects are conditional on the posterior mode of the variance parameters, and each variance keeps its own posterior. print(), summary(), backend_decision() and fb_plan() say so. On 12 simulated trials (26 variance parameters) every per-trial variance ASReml 4.2 identifies is within 0.17 of its ASReml standard error, and the fit takes 8 seconds. Other models past 15 are still refused by hyperparam_budget. backend = "auto" fits these models on INLA, where it used brms.

  • predict(fit, classify = "gen") now works when gen is random, on INLA and brms fits. Each genotype’s prediction is the fixed part, averaged over the other fixed factors, plus its random effect, with a posterior SD and credible interval. On a multi-environment fit with gen:env also random, classify = "gen" adds each genotype’s gen:env effects averaged over environments, and classify = "gen:env" returns one value per genotype and environment, including combinations with no plots. This matches ASReml’s default predict(). On two field trials (john.alpha and 16 genotypes of besag.met) the predictions differ from ASReml’s by at most 0.11 SE for genotypes and 0.4 SE for genotype-by-county cells, and the posterior SDs are 1-25% wider than ASReml’s SEs, because they include the uncertainty in the variance components. With the variance components held at ASReml’s estimates, the predictions agree to 0.006 SE and the SDs to 0.3%.

  • The arguments of ASReml’s predict() that change those rules, such as present, average and ignore, or ask for sed or vcov, now stop with the error classify_argument_not_supported instead of being ignored.

  • at(f, level):g fits on both engines. The random effect g applies only where f takes the named levels, with one variance per level, as in ASReml. at(design, "split"):mainplot gives a main-plot variance to the split-plot trials alone. Levels can be named by value or by position in levels(f), and a level the data lack is refused (at_level_not_in_data). On simulated split-plot and RCB trials the main-plot SD was within 1% of ASReml’s on INLA and 3% on brms.

  • at(trial):ar1(row):ar1(col) fits a separate AR1 x AR1 field on each trial on INLA, with its own SD and both correlations, reported as sd_spatial__trial<level>, rho_row__trial<level> and rho_col__trial<level>. at(trial, "T2"):ar1(row):ar1(col) fits the field on the named trials only. On three simulated trials every posterior median was within 0.3 posterior SDs of ASReml’s estimate. brms refuses the term.

  • residual = ~ ar1(row):ar1(col) fits ASReml’s separable residual with no nugget on INLA, for a Gaussian response: three parameters, and no sigma row. residual = ~ dsum(~ ar1(row):ar1(col) | trial) fits it separately in each trial. The random-side random = ~ ar1(row):ar1(col) keeps its nugget, so the two models are told apart by where they are written. On a simulated 16 x 10 trial the field SD and the two correlations were within 1.4% of ASReml’s.

Fixes to INLA results

  • The median and 95% limits of each variance component in summary(fit)$varcomp are now read from INLA’s marginal of the log precision, not of the precision. Standard deviations near zero were overstated before: on one field-trial fit the median of the row term fell from 0.123 to 0.009, matching INLA’s summary.hyperpar quantiles converted to the standard-deviation scale. Variance components saved from earlier versions will differ from a refit.

  • fb_variance_draws() and vpredict() now draw the variance components jointly with each component’s distribution taken from INLA’s stored marginal, so the median and 95% limits of the draws equal those in summary(fit)$varcomp. Earlier draws differed from them by up to about 1%.

  • vcov() on an INLA fit is now computed from INLA’s Gaussian approximation with no random draws. It was estimated from random draws before and varied between calls. Two calls now give the same matrix. n_samples is still accepted and ignored.

  • fb_as_draws_simple() on an INLA fit draws with R’s random number generator from INLA’s stored approximation, so set.seed() before the call gives the same draws every time. INLA’s own sampler does not repeat under a seed. The draws match it in distribution.

  • fb_plan() no longer reports that a model will not fit on data under 100,000 rows because the memory check cannot size one of its terms. flexybayes() skips that check below 100,000 rows.

New: a flag for weakly identified variance components

  • On INLA fits, a variance component whose 95% posterior interval covers 40% or more of its prior’s probability is marked weakly identified in the note column of summary(fit)$varcomp, and the fit warns. Data that inform a component narrow it to a small share of the prior, and a share this large means the reported value mostly reflects the prior. It is common with a grouping factor of three or four levels, or a random term with the same grouping as a fixed factor. brms fits are not checked yet. Silence the warning with options(flexyBayes.silence_weak_identification_warning = TRUE).

  • The warning that a random slope has collapsed to zero now compares the slope’s standard deviation times its covariate’s standard deviation with 1% of the residual standard deviation, so the result no longer depends on the covariate’s units.

For packages that extend flexyBayes

  • fb_register_refusals() lets another package add its own refusal codes from its .onLoad(), in a partition under its own name, and fb_refuse() raises any registered code as a flexybayes_refusal condition. fb_refusals() gains a package column, and every refusal condition records the package that registered its code.

  • fb_marginal_cov() returns the marginal covariance of the response of a fit over given rows: one block per variance component with its design and structure, the Kronecker factors of an AR1 x AR1 field, the residual, and any known variance or covariance. as.matrix() gives the dense matrix. Each variance is its posterior mean, the squared estimate plus the squared standard error of that component in summary(fit)$varcomp.

  • fb_refit() refits the model of a fit on new data, keeping its random terms, family, priors, engine settings, weights, offsets and known variance. It can add fixed columns, and on brms it can take extra prior rows, Stan code and a hook that edits the formula. emit_brms() loses its nl_block argument, which formula_hook replaces.

  • fb_isolated_lapply() runs each call of a function in its own R process, as options(flexyBayes.isolation = "process") does for a fit: values, messages and warnings come back in job order, and a process that ends without returning is the refusal isolated_process_died.

  • fb_extension_api() gives the version of the functions a package reads a fit through, 1 in this release. ?fb_extension documents them: fb_model_terms(), fb_response_values(), fb_offset_values(), fb_model_weights(), fb_known_variance(), fb_engine_settings(), fb_convergence(), fb_inla_posterior_sample(), fb_check_refit() and fb_fixed_design(). fb_as_draws_simple() gains a method for a brms fit.

  • Prior rows passed to fb_refit(extra_prior = ) are recorded in the model manifest with the source extra_prior.

Other fixes

  • fb_plan() refuses an argument it does not take with plan_argument_unknown. A misspelt name used to fall into its unused ... and the plan was made for a different model.

  • The flexybayes_stream() help now says that with prior = NULL each random-effect standard deviation takes the package’s half-normal default and the fixed effects keep INLA’s defaults. It used to say the backend’s defaults were used for every parameter.

  • On brms, prior_vc_sd now sets lognormal(0, prior_vc_sd) on the standard deviation of an interaction random effect such as a:b or a:b:c. A three-way term used to stop with “‘length = 3’ in coercion to ‘logical(1)’”, because term$var partially matched the term’s vars, and a two-way term was left at brms’s default prior.

  • On INLA, prior_vc_sd now sets lognormal(0, prior_vc_sd) on a three-way random term such as a:b:c, as brms does. The term used to get the package’s half-normal default, because the legacy prior list left out multi-way interactions.

  • A non-Gaussian INLA fit with a three-way random term no longer warns “partial match of ‘var’ to ‘vars’” under options(warnPartialMatchDollar = TRUE). The covariate standardisation now reads the term’s fields by exact name.

  • With gen fixed and gen:env random, predict(classify = "gen") now includes the gen:env effects, as ASReml does. It used to return the fixed part only, with SEs 8-11% wider than ASReml’s on besag.met.

  • fb_plan() names an AR1 field term as it was written, for example ar1(row):ar1(col), in its representation plan. It printed (ar1_spatial | ?) for every field.

  • The INLA hyperparameter count now has one precision per section of a dsum(~ units | f) residual. It counted the residual as one, so with 12 trials it read 16 where INLA has 26, and a residual over many sections could pass the limit of 15 unrefused.

  • The print of an INLA fit with a dsum() residual names its family once instead of once per section.

  • The gate’s warning above 10 hyperparameters no longer says that a ccd integration is set. Nothing set it.

  • A saved INLA fit holds only the fit. The formula and INLA’s prior functions kept the frame the model was fitted in, with the data and the engine’s working copies, so saveRDS() of a 10,368-plot fit wrote 1,119 MB in 93 s. It now writes 160 MB in 17 s, and a job of fb_isolated_lapply() that is given the fit runs in 3.7 s instead of 7.4 s with about a quarter of the memory. Results are unchanged.

  • The two correlations of an AR1 x AR1 field are now named after the factor each runs along, rho_<factor>, in summary()$varcomp, print(), fb_variance_draws(), vpredict() and the per-level names of at(trial):ar1(row):ar1(col) and dsum(~ ar1(row):ar1(col) | trial). ar1(col):ar1(row) and ar1(row):ar1(col) now report the same correlation under the same name, as the field panel and ASReml (ar1(row):ar1(col)!row!cor) already did. Previously rho_row was the correlation along whichever factor the term wrote first.

  • vcov(), predict(se.fit = TRUE), predict(classify = ) and the posterior draws of an INLA fit with a smooth beside the intercept, such as random = ~ site + spl(x), stopped with “leading principal minor … is not positive” in 18 of 40 simulated fits of one such design. The smooth and the intercept share a constant that only the smooth’s sum-to-zero constraint fixes, so the precision INLA stores is singular in that direction and rounding can make its factorisation fail. These calls now condition on the constraint the way INLA::inla.posterior.sample() does, and on such a fit the vcov() SDs agree with INLA’s summary.fixed to 5e-6 and with 100,000 of INLA’s own posterior draws to within 0.5 Monte Carlo standard errors. Fits whose precision factorises give the same results as before.

  • A fit whose stored precision is singular in a direction no constraint fixes is refused by name, inla_config_precision_not_positive_definite.

  • A fixed or random term that names a column not in the data is refused before any engine runs, with model_variable_not_in_data and the missing names in variables. It used to stop with R’s “object ‘x’ not found”, on INLA only after the fit had run.

  • A response that is a factor or character vector is refused with response_not_numeric on both engines and in fb_plan(). A three-level factor used to be fitted on INLA as a Gaussian on its level codes 1 to 3. A binomial response keeps its own refusal, binomial_response_not_binary, which fb_plan() now reports too.

  • The bar grammar fits a transformed response, log(y) ~ x + (1 | g), as the ASReml grammar does. The two fits agree to within the spread of two identical INLA calls (1e-8 in the coefficients), and the coefficients agree with lme4::lmer() to 2e-4.

  • aggregate = "foo" (aggregate_argument_invalid), weights that are not one number per row (weights_invalid), a prior that is not an fb_prior() object (prior_not_fb_prior) and a flexybayes_stream() source that is not a file, a data frame or a chunk generator (stream_source_invalid) are refused by name. They used to stop untyped, and a character prior crashed with “$ operator is invalid for atomic vectors”.

  • The refusals of the aggregated and streamed routes are flexybayes_refusal conditions with a registered reason_code. A model the aggregation plan cannot compress refuses with aggregation_plan_ineligible, its reasons in reason_codes, and a model outside the aggregated or streamed route’s scope with aggregation_out_of_scope, its reason in scope_reason.

  • fb_plan(aggregate = TRUE) reports no route where the fit refuses aggregate = TRUE, for example a Poisson model with a continuous covariate. It used to plan a per-row fit.

  • predict() on an INLA fit takes re_formula and summary. Its predictions are population-level, so re_formula = NA returns the fixed part of the model, as on a brms fit. Any other re_formula, and summary = FALSE, are refused with method_argument_not_supported. vcov() and fb_as_draws_simple() on a brms fit refuse n_samples, which they used to ignore.

  • update() with no change now re-fits under the prior the fit ran under. When the original call stated a prior or prior_vc_sd but not prior_fixed_sd, the re-fit put a normal(0, 100) prior on every fixed effect, which the original fit did not have. The re-fit also records its data under the name the fit recorded.

  • vpredict() works on a flexyBayes fit when sommer is attached after flexyBayes. sommer’s own vpredict() used to mask it and stop with “no applicable method”.

  • A brms fit finished with proceed() after review_code = TRUE carries the record of the direct call: its known variance, missing-response policy, backend and aggregation setting, the routing decision and the prior record. It used to lack them, so update() on it refitted without the known variance.

Minor improvements

  • vcov(), predict(se.fit = TRUE) and predict(classify = ) on an INLA fit take about half the time (4.7 s to 2.2 s on a 10,368-plot fit with 79 hyperparameter configurations): each configuration’s precision matrix is factorised on the ordering of the first, which gives the same factor. Results are identical.

Documentation

  • New vignette, Moving from ASReml-R: the flexyBayes spelling of each ASReml construct the package supports (fixed, random, residual, at(), diag(), us(), ar1(), dsum(), weights, predict(classify = ), vpredict(), summary()$varcomp), the constructs it refuses and why, and how to read a posterior summary beside a REML one. Every ASReml number on the page comes from a stored fit, so it builds without an ASReml licence.

  • Moving from ASReml-R shows the 0.16.0 additions beside stored ASReml 4.2 fits: predict(classify = "gen") with gen random, at(f, level):g, the nugget-free residual = ~ ar1(row):ar1(col), a separate field per trial with at(trial):ar1(row):ar1(col), per-trial genotype and residual variances on 12 trials fitted by empirical Bayes, and predict(allow_new_levels = TRUE, mean_by = ) for a county the fit did not see. Its list of refused models no longer includes at(env, "C1"):gen or the nugget-free residual, which both fit.

  • inst/TRANSLATION.md lists per-trial genotype and residual variances, prediction with a random classify factor, and prediction at new levels, each with its ASReml comparison. inst/KNOWN_ISSUES.md adds two open issues: the weak-identification flag can stay silent where REML cannot identify a variance, and ar1(t):g reports its correlation as rho_row.

Tests

  • flexyBayes is now compared with stored ASReml 4.2 fits on all eight model shapes of the ASReml oracle suite, up from one. On the six shapes fitted on INLA the fixed effects agree to within 0.011 of ASReml’s standard error and every variance component ASReml identifies agrees to within 9% (the tolerance is 15%). The replicate variance of john.alpha, which ASReml estimates with a standard error larger than itself, is flagged weakly identified in all three shapes that carry it. us(env):gen is refused on INLA by name, and on brms its fixed effects and identified variances agree.

flexyBayes 0.15.0

A feature release for two-stage analyses of a series of trials and for selection runs. A second stage can take the full covariance of the first stage’s estimates, selection runs expose their fold data, a shrinkage prior can be confined to the candidate covariates, and parallel fold workers run as separate R processes. No model family or engine is added.

Two-stage analysis

  • flexybayes(known_variance = K) takes a symmetric positive-definite covariance matrix with one row per data row, for a second stage whose first stage returned the full covariance of its estimates: Var(y) = sigma^2 I + K. INLA fits K as a latent effect with precision K^-1. brms refuses a matrix with known_variance_not_supported, because its fcor() term fits sigma^2 K and does not combine with se().

  • fb_select(covariance = "base_model") on such a base whitens each fold by sigma^2 I + sum_k sigma_k^2 Z_k Z_k' + K, with K in full.

  • fb_select(refit = list(method = "bayes")) runs on an INLA base with a known variance or covariance: each fold is refitted with it, and each held-out row’s known variance is added to its predictive variance.

  • fb_select(keep_fold_data = TRUE) keeps each fold’s whitened data, read by three new functions: fb_select_fold_data() returns the whitened and protected-removed design of each fold, fb_select_path() solves the penalised path again at the run’s alpha or another, and fb_select_refit() refits a named column set by generalised least squares and scores its held-out clusters. New refusal code selection_fold_data_not_kept.

  • fb_variance_draws() draws an INLA fit’s variance components jointly, under the names and on the scale of summary(fit)$varcomp.

  • model.matrix() on a fit takes newdata, coding its factors on the fitted data’s levels with columns in the order of coef().

Shrinkage on a block of candidates

  • regularized_horseshoe() and r2d2() take scope = "block", which keeps protected fixed effects out of the shrinkage prior. The reference model of fb_select() is fitted as the brms non-linear formula y ~ a + b: part a holds the intercept, the protected effects and the random terms under the base model’s priors, and part b ~ 0 + <candidates> carries the prior. The block must hold every candidate. Coefficients, tidy(), confint(), draws and the shrinkage factors use the candidates’ own names. A known variance per row (known_variance) is carried when no out-of-fold score is asked for. The projection decision refuses on this scope, and decision = "auto" resolves to "full". A model with a variable named a or b refuses with penalty_block_part_name_taken.

Selection folds

  • With more than one fold worker (options(flexyBayes.selection_workers)), fb_select() runs each fold in a separate R process started through callr, instead of forking the session. A forked worker of a session with INLA, OpenMP and TBB loaded had died with SIGABRT in R’s garbage collector with memory to spare. options(flexyBayes.isolation = "fork") keeps the forked workers. Without callr, more than one worker refuses with isolation_requires_callr.
  • The refusal for a forked fold worker that ends without a result (selection_parallel_worker_failed) states what was seen, and names memory and a crash in compiled code only as possible causes.
  • INLA refits inside fb_select()’s fold loops compute only what the fold reads: no DIC, WAIC or latent marginals, posterior configurations only where draws are taken, and no second fit testing an AR1 field. The stored fold fit is about 12 times smaller, and a fold whose field the data do not support no longer fits twice.
  • On INLA, the posterior predictive draws that score a fold are taken for the held-out rows only, so a draw no longer holds the whole latent field.
  • The Bayesian route scores each fold on 8,000 predictive draws, up from 4,000. On an 800-row, 20-site example with a weak candidate effect, the Monte Carlo standard deviation of a between-model elpd difference was 0.26 nats at 4,000 draws against a difference of 0.81, and 0.12 at 8,000. Sampling 16,000 draws for one fold took 28 s against 20 s for 500.

Other fixes

  • prior_summary() returns the flexyBayes summary when brms is attached after flexyBayes. brms re-exports the rstantools generic, whose default returned NULL. The methods are registered on it too.
  • The README install block also installs remotes, knitr and rmarkdown, which building the vignettes needs.
  • Vignette 03 reads the number of refusal codes from fb_refusals() when it is built.
  • A build from a git worktree no longer ships its .git file.
  • The vignettes open with what each one covers.

flexyBayes 0.14.5

A patch release for fits with an AR1 field. The field’s standard deviation now has the package’s default prior, and whether the data support the field is tested against a fit without it. No model family, engine or exported function is added.

  • On INLA, the standard deviation of an AR1 field (ar1(t), ar1(row):ar1(col), id(trial):ar1(row):ar1(col) and ar1(t):g) now has the default half-normal prior, as every other random-effect standard deviation does. It had INLA’s own prior, log-gamma(1, 5e-05) on the precision, and the model manifest recorded it as an engine default. A stated prior reaches the field as fb_prior(sd(group = "spatial") ~ half_normal(scale = s)).
  • The field’s correlations keep INLA’s own prior, and the manifest still records them as engine defaults.
  • A fit with an AR1 field is now also fitted without the field, and the two marginal likelihoods are compared. When the model without the field is favoured by a Bayes factor of more than 100 to 1, the fit warns that the field is not supported by the data, and summary(fit)$varcomp marks the sd_spatial row collapsed. The field SD can no longer show this on its own: on data with no spatial signal it now reads about 0.9 beside a nugget of 0.8.
  • On simulated 10 x 8 grids, 13 per setting, the warning fired on all 13 grids with no field, on none of the 26 grids with a field SD of 1 or 1.5 (nugget 0.5 and 0.3), and on 11 of the 13 grids with a field SD of 0.4 beside a nugget of 1. In every one of the 52 cases it agreed with a REML likelihood-ratio test at the 5% level, which also finds no field on those 11 weak-field grids.
  • The fit without the field adds about 1.3 s on 80 plots, roughly doubling the time of a small fit. It is not run when the 95% interval of a field correlation excludes zero. print(fit) and summary(fit) show the log Bayes factor under the field block, and fit$extras$field_test holds the value, the threshold and the verdict.

flexyBayes 0.14.4

A maintenance release. No model family, penalty family, engine or exported function is added, and no fit changes.

  • The help page of fb_log_posterior() now defines the log_normalizer attribute as log Z, the log of the integral of the unnormalised density. It said -log Z, the opposite of what proxymix 0.16.0 reads. No backend returns a finite value yet, so no result changes.
  • The grouped penalty families in ?fb_penalty are now a bulleted list, and seven source lines longer than 80 characters are wrapped, so lintr reports no lints.

flexyBayes 0.14.3

A patch release for repeatable INLA fits. Identical calls now agree closely on the variance components. No model family, penalty family, engine or exported function is added.

INLA threads

  • Every INLA fit now runs on one thread, num.threads = "1:1", on the per-row, aggregated and streamed routes and in every fold of fb_select(). At INLA’s own default, "10:1" on a 10-core machine, identical calls returned different variance components where a variance is weakly informed: on a 48-trial barley model with 22 localities, eight identical fits at "4:1" gave the locality variance from 0.58 to 42.3, and at "1:1" from 0.75 to 0.79, with the fixed effects unchanged. This is a change in behaviour. INLA::inla.setOption(num.threads = ) no longer sets the plan of a flexyBayes fit. options(flexyBayes.inla_threads = "4:1") does, and "inla" returns the choice to INLA.
  • A fold worker of fb_select() no longer sets INLA’s threads to cores %/% workers, which replaced the plan the caller had chosen.

flexyBayes 0.14.2

A patch release for selection on a weighted base. fb_select() carries the base model’s observation weights on every route, re-estimates them in each fold on request, selects on a padded field whose added cells have no response, and runs a shared AR1 x AR1 field under prediction = "new_cluster". No model family, penalty family, engine or exported function is added. One change in behaviour: a weighted base on the projection decision now refuses, where 0.14.1 selected on the unweighted model without a message.

Observation weights in selection

  • A base fitted with weights is selected with residual variance sigma^2 / w on each training row and sigma^2 on each held-out row, on the REML plug-in, on covariance = "base_model", on the penalised optimiser and its stability subsamples, and in every Bayesian fold refit, which is fitted with the weights of its rows. 0.14.1 selected a weighted base on the REML plug-in route as if it had no weights, and said nothing. The fold covariance read no weights, and R/selection_weights.R was called from no selection route. The certificate records where the weights were absorbed.
  • The projection decision refuses a weighted base (selection_weights_not_carried) instead of selecting unweighted. This is a change in behaviour.
  • fb_resamples(weights_by = ~ group) re-estimates the weights in each fold from the training rows alone. The base is refitted without weights on the training rows, s2 of a group is the mean squared residual of its rows with the random effects included, the group’s weight is median(s2) / s2, and held-out rows get weight 1. Each fold’s weights are recorded on the certificate. The base must have been fitted with weights (selection_weights_by_unweighted_base).

Missing responses and the shared field

  • On the benchmark and optimiser workflows, a row with a missing response, such as a cell fb_complete_grid() adds to pad a field, is neither fitted nor scored in any fold. The fold covariance is built on the full lattice and restricted to the rows with a response, which is the exact marginal for a Gaussian response. selection_missing_response_not_carried is withdrawn from the registry. A fold whose held-out units have no response still refuses by name.
  • id(g):ar1(row):ar1(col) runs under prediction = "new_cluster". A held-out level of g gets a field independent of the training levels, with the shared variance and correlations, so its cross-covariance with the training rows is zero. A field with no replicating factor, and vm() and ped() terms, keep the refusal.
  • Under new_cluster, the Bayesian refit keeps each held-out trial on one field label: the position factors of TRIAL:RANGE and TRIAL:ROW are relabelled with the trial, and the rows the fold cannot estimate are relabelled the same way. Before, the refit refused on some folds of a weighted field base and not on others.

Refusal registry

  • 231 typed codes: selection_weights_not_carried and selection_weights_by_unweighted_base added, selection_missing_response_not_carried withdrawn.

flexyBayes 0.14.1

A patch release that fits the ASReml spellings of a shared AR1 x AR1 field and of aliased fixed effects the way ASReml 4.2 does, and makes penalised selection converge on grouped candidates. Two changes can stop a model that fitted in 0.14.0: at(trial):ar1(row):ar1(col) now refuses, and id(trial) is the spelling of the shared field. flexybayes() refuses fixed-effect columns the data do not estimate unless fixed_alias = "drop" is given.

Models written as in ASReml

  • id(trial):ar1(row):ar1(col) fits one AR1 x AR1 field per trial on INLA, with the variance and both correlations shared across trials, as in ASReml. at(trial):ar1(row):ar1(col), which ASReml fits with separate parameters for each trial, now refuses (at_field_per_level_parameters_not_fitted). 0.14.0 fitted the shared field under that spelling. A brms plan reports will_fit = FALSE when the brms fit would refuse the model.
  • fb_select(covariance = "base_model") builds the fold covariance of id(trial):ar1(row):ar1(col), one AR1 x AR1 field per trial with the two correlations and the variance shared across trials. The covariance is factored one trial at a time at any size.
  • flexybayes() now refuses a model whose fixed-effect columns are not all estimated by the rows with a response, as in a factorial with empty cells, and names the columns (fixed_effects_aliased). Before, INLA and brms fitted such a model without a message and reported those columns at their prior. This is a change in behaviour: a model that fitted in 0.14.0 can refuse. fixed_alias = "drop" fits it on INLA as asreml 4.2 does, with the aliased columns fixed at zero and listed in fit$extras$fixed_alias, and predict() returns NA with status "Aliased" for a cell the fitting rows do not estimate.
  • fb_select(protected_alias = "drop") fits a protected term whose columns are not all identified on a fold’s training rows, as an unbalanced VARIETY * NAPPLIED * SEEDRATE is, the way ASReml 4.2 does: each fold drops the columns asreml reports as aliased, a held-out row whose cell the training rows do not estimate is not scored, and the certificate lists both per fold. The default, "refuse", is unchanged.
  • fb_select(protected_alias = "drop") now works with refit = list(method = "bayes"): each fold’s refit leaves out that fold’s dropped columns, and value$not_estimable counts the held-out rows left out of the log predictive density. With covariance = "base_model", each fold’s refit fixes its aliased protected columns at zero instead of fitting them at their prior.

Penalised selection

  • fb_decision() gains n_lambda and lambda_min_ratio, which set the penalised optimiser’s path grid. The defaults, 20 points down to 1e-3 of each fold’s lambda_max, are the grid 0.14.0 used. The grid is printed by fb_select() and its plan, and recorded on the certificate as benchmark$glmnet$path_grid.
  • group_lasso() gains alpha (default 1). Below one it is a group elastic net: (alpha / scale) sum_g sqrt(p_g) ||beta_g|| plus ((1 - alpha) / (2 scale)) ||beta||^2, and a group still enters or leaves whole.
  • Group lasso and group elastic net path points are solved by block coordinate descent with an exact update for each group. The other grouped families keep the proximal-gradient solver.
  • A grouped-family path point is accepted when its KKT residual is at most 1e-6 times the largest entry of |A'z| on the fold’s whitened payload, in place of an absolute 1e-6, so the threshold follows the response’s units. Ridge, Laplace and elastic net keep the absolute 1e-6. The threshold and the solver of each point are recorded in the optimiser arm’s kkt table.
  • Exclusive lasso and group-exclusive path points on blocks of strongly correlated candidates now reach their exact optimum. In 0.14.0 such a point could stop after 200,000 iterations and refuse with selection_prox_mode_not_converged.

Reporting

  • glance() on an fb_select() result names its out-of-fold scores as losses. metric, protected_only, full and improvement are now loss, loss_protected_only, loss_full and loss_reduction. Lower is better, and loss_reduction is positive when the candidates improve prediction. On the Bayesian workflow the loss is neg_elpd, minus the log predictive density of a held-out unit, where the old metric column said elpd. print() labels the same block “out-of-fold loss”.
  • The default-prior note, the printed INLA formula and prior_summary() say which scale the default prior is on. A Gaussian INLA fit runs on the standardised response, and its priors are shown on that scale and on the response, for example half-normal-SD(5) beside half-normal-SD(3.235). A lognormal prior on the standardised response, previously shown as a half-normal, is shown as a lognormal.

Authors

  • Anabel Forte Deltell is listed as an author again, in DESCRIPTION, inst/CITATION, CITATION.cff and codemeta.json.

flexyBayes 0.14.0

The release for a two-stage analysis of a designed multi-environment trial. Penalised selection can now take its fold covariance from a refit of the base model, carry known first-stage variances into the second stage, value the support the optimiser chose by held-out log predictive density, and rank declared blocks by what removing each one costs in held-out loss. Each engine fit and each fold can run in its own process. One internal function is removed, and the statements the package makes about INLA and brms are checked against the engines.

Selection for a two-stage design

  • fb_select() gains covariance = "base_model", which reads the fold covariance of the benchmark and optimiser workflows from a refit of the base model on each fold’s training rows. It builds random slopes, diag(f):g, a single-trial ar1(row):ar1(col) field and vm() or ped() known covariances, and factors a covariance that is block-diagonal over a grouping one block at a time.
  • The default, covariance = "reml_plugin", is unchanged below a stated memory bound, options(flexyBayes.selection_dense_gb = ) (0.5 GiB, 8,192 rows). Above it, a covariance that would be formed as a dense matrix refuses with selection_dense_covariance_too_large instead of exhausting memory.
  • flexybayes(known_variance = v) adds a known variance to each row’s residual variance, Var(y_i) = sigma^2 + v_i, for the second stage of a two-stage analysis. brms fits it as se(sqrt(v), sigma = TRUE) and INLA as a row effect with known variance. fb_select(covariance = "base_model") carries it into the fold covariance, and the routes that would leave it out refuse with known_variance_not_supported.
  • fb_select(refit = list(method = "bayes")) refits the support the penalised optimiser chose on each fold as a Bayesian model on the base’s own engine, scores each held-out row by its log predictive density, and reports the per-unit sums, their total with its standard error across units, and the share of between-trial variance a declared block explains. glance(x, against = y) differences two such runs unit by unit.
  • The Bayesian workflow’s fold refits now keep a base’s prior_vc_sd and prior_fixed_sd. Before, they ran under the package’s default priors.
  • fb_select(ablation = TRUE) drops each declared block of the penalised path in turn, walks the path again on the same folds, and reports in tidy(level = "group") the change in held-out loss per unit with its standard error, and the change in log predictive density where refit = list(method = "bayes") ran. The read-out is not nested.

Selection read-outs

  • Entrance read-outs for penalised selection. tidy() adds entry_s_median, the point on s by which half of the folds able to estimate a column had admitted it, with its quartiles and their spread. It is the point plot(type = "entrance_path") labels, and path_entry_s keeps its meaning, the earliest entry on any fold. tidy(level = "group") gives the same profile for a grouped penalty’s groups and for declared penalty blocks. plot(type = "entrance_heatmap") shows the share of folds holding each candidate or group along s, and the entrance path now uses a logarithmic s axis so its labels no longer overprint. fb_decision(stability_subsamples = ) adds subsample stability selection (Meinshausen and Buhlmann 2010) over half-samples of the resampling unit. It is off by default, and plan = TRUE states its cost.
  • Two displays. plot(fit, type = "spatial_field") draws the posterior mean of an ar1(row):ar1(col) field on the trial’s row-by-column array, titled with the trial identifier the caller gives. On a selection, plot(x, type = "loss_surface", alongside = list(...)) draws the out-of-fold loss over s and the elastic-net mixing parameter from results run at other mixing values on the same score contract, with each result’s chosen point marked. It needs plotly, now in Suggests.

Fitting in a separate process

  • options(flexyBayes.isolation = "process") runs each engine fit, and each fold of fb_select(), in a separate R process started through callr (in Suggests). If that process is killed, the call refuses with isolated_process_died, naming the engine, the function called and the signal or exit status, and the session carries on. The default, "none", fits in the session as before.

Refusals and corrections

  • A brms::bf() object with a non-linear formula, a formula or fixed value for a distributional parameter, or a family other than the family argument now refuses with brms_ingest_feature_unsupported. Before, both engines fitted bf(y ~ x + (1 | g), sigma ~ x) without sigma ~ x and fitted the family argument in place of a family named inside bf(), and nl = TRUE stopped with an untyped error.
  • fb_select() refuses a base whose data have a missing response when the unpenalised benchmark, the penalised optimiser or benchmark = TRUE is asked for (selection_missing_response_not_carried). It used to stop inside the optimiser with an untyped error.
  • The refusal raised when refit = list(method = "bayes") meets a path that froze no support no longer carries the penalty family’s name as one of its condition classes. A ridge path’s refusal was classed flexybayes_refusal_selection_refit_support_undefined and ridge. The second class is gone, and the family is carried as data on the condition.
  • At s = 1 the penalised optimiser’s support is now empty, as the exact solution there is. Rounding left values of order 1e-16 that counted as selected, so a one-standard-error choice of s = 1 could report columns in the chosen support and in tidy()$retained.

What the package states about the engines

  • Refusals, the capability table and the help pages no longer describe a gap in flexyBayes as a limit of INLA or brms. Two such statements were false: brms writes a multi-trait covariance with a known relationship matrix, and INLA has an exchangeable group model. Statements about the engines that remain are checked against the engines in test-engine-claims.R.
  • corh(f):g now refuses by name on INLA as it does on brms, and the INLA refusal of a model the brms route also refuses no longer points at brms.

Documentation and messages

  • The README keeps what the package does, how to install it, one worked example, the table of models at least one engine fits, and where to read more. The row notes, and the structures neither engine fits, are in KNOWN_ISSUES.md.
  • A two-stage analysis of a series of trials is a new page. It fits each trial of a simulated series on its own, carries the first stage’s variances into the second with known_variance, whitens the folds from a refit of that second-stage model, and reports what each declared block of trial-level covariates costs when it is dropped.
  • Mixed models in brief and Bayesian estimation in brief are rebuilt and show the half-normal default prior. Selecting over a candidate block is rebuilt on this release.
  • The default-prior message printed on a first fit is two sentences.

Removals

  • The internal cross-engine comparison triangulate(), with triangulate_genomic() and triangulate_gwas(), is removed. Nothing in the package called it, and agreement between two engines fitted from one parsed model cannot detect a translation error both share.

flexyBayes 0.13.1

A patch release for penalised selection. It adds two read-outs of a penalised path and holds every point on the path to one optimality certificate. No model family, penalty family, engine or exported function is added.

Selection read-outs

  • plot(fit, type = "entrance_path") draws the out-of-fold score along s = lambda / lambda_max, from the strongest penalty to the weakest, and labels each candidate at its median first entry: the point by which at least half of the folds that could estimate it had admitted it. A candidate admitted on fewer than half of those folds is not labelled, and candidates entering at the same point share one label. The ordinate is the mean of the per-unit scores, for example RMSE, and is not an inclusion probability. ridge() and exclusive_lasso() have no finite null anchor and so no s coordinate, and the display says so.
  • augment(fit, type = "assessment_predictions") returns the stored out-of-fold predictions behind the optimiser’s decision: one row per assessment row and repeat, with the row’s position in the data, its fold, repeat and scoring unit, the observed and predicted values on the modelled scale after any Gaussian offset, the selected tuning point and the hash of the decision-stage score contract. It does not predict rows supplied by the caller. The default, type = "unit_scores", returns the per-unit scores as before.

Optimality certificates

  • Every optimiser path point is held to one KKT threshold of 1e-6, whichever provider computed it. glmnet stops on a change in its own objective, and on strongly correlated blocks, or when it runs out of iterations, it returns points above that threshold, and 0.13.0 scored those points as if they were the optimum. Such a point is now solved again, on the support glmnet found or by the internal proximal solver, and refused by name (selection_prox_mode_not_converged) if neither certifies it. On correlated synthetic designs this turned residuals of up to 2.6 into certified points and left the selected supports unchanged.
  • Grouped path points were held to 1e-9 and could be refused on a large correlated block after 200,000 iterations. They now use the same 1e-6 threshold. On exclusive-lasso paths over correlated synthetic blocks, every support accepted at 1e-6 matched the exact optimum from an independent quadratic-programming solver, out-of-fold predictions moved by less than 1e-5 response standard deviations, and the paths ran 3 to 16 times faster. The lower-level solvers keep their stricter defaults.

Documentation

  • ?fb_penalty states that under treatment contrasts a factor’s group holds its non-reference contrast columns, and the reference level has no design column. The exclusive lasso encourages one member of a declared block of correlated alternatives to represent it and does not guarantee a single survivor.

flexyBayes 0.13.0

This release makes the selection and large-MET substrate materially safer and more reproducible. It is sufficient for the model-fitting and variable- selection stages of the planned nert workflow. Study-specific data assembly, the M0–M2 orchestration and reporting remain in the study repository.

Selection at scale

  • fb_select() now exposes lasso, elastic net, group lasso, sparse group lasso, exclusive lasso and the group-exclusive composite through the explicitly frequentist penalized_optimizer workflow. Grouped penalties use the package’s proximal provider and do not pass through the brms prior compiler. Bayesian requests for optimiser-only families still refuse by name.
  • Every penalised fit records the relative path coordinate s = lambda / lambda_max, fold-specific lambdas, complete support histories (entry, exit, re-entry and availability), KKT/proximal diagnostics and the grouping map. Protected terms remain outside the penalty.
  • Candidate spaces and learned transformations are compiled inside each training fold. Rank-deficient candidates, assessment-only factor levels and representations that cannot carry a fold-local drop have typed outcomes. Score contracts and certificates hash the actual folds, responses and design values.
  • Fold evaluation can run concurrently. Serial and concurrent runs preserve exact folds, model order, selected support, scores and certificate content. The measured three-worker pilot was 2.35 times faster than serial and used about 11.5 GiB aggregate memory. Worker death is a typed refusal. Choose the number of workers by available memory, not by core count.

Model and data integrity

  • The default variance-component and residual-scale prior is now half-normal on the standard deviation, with a common scale convention across engines. Audits no longer claim support merely because a bounded-uniform prior was stated when an INLA approximation escaped that support.
  • Non-Gaussian INLA fits standardise numeric covariates and carry the transformation into predictions and reported coefficients.
  • Family objects and character family names now pass through one exact family/link gate. Unsupported families, contradictory links and invalid response domains refuse before an engine runs.
  • Factor-analytic GxE is conservatively refused on both engines because repeated identical fits did not satisfy the release’s repeatability gate. Known-covariance block carriers are likewise refused. Use the equivalent precision carrier. These are deliberate correctness boundaries, not claims that complex MET covariance modelling is complete.
  • Missing-response augmentation continues to preserve design nodes. Posterior equivalence with omission requires ignorability and a common prior on the same parameters. Backend defaults that depend on the realised design do not establish that condition automatically.
  • Streaming, aggregation, family support, link handling and parallel-worker failures now use typed refusals. Fits record provider versions, threads, seeds and relevant reproducibility metadata.
  • Deferred brms review objects now preserve the caller’s seed and control settings when proceed() executes the reviewed model. Earlier builds kept the draw counts but silently fell back to backend defaults for those two settings.
  • When a host supplies no detectable core count, an INLA fit now receives the conservative num.threads = "1:1" setting instead of INLA’s malformed NA:1 default and undocumented parser fallback. Explicit caller settings and valid host defaults are unchanged. Some INLA builds still print their own hardware-probe messages. These are recorded as an upstream environment note and are not suppressed as package warnings.

API consolidation

  • fb_brms() is deprecated in favour of flexybayes(..., backend = "brms"). fb_engine() is deprecated in favour of direct fitting arguments, or a named sampler-settings list in fb_select(engine = ).
  • fb_from_asreml() and fb_from_brms() are deprecated in favour of fb_plan() for inspection. The compatibility functions still return their historical objects and warn with class flexybayes_deprecated.
  • The earlier deprecations of fb(), fb_inla(), is_fb_cov(), is_fb_approx(), is_fb_engine(), cat_code() and proceed() remain in their warning-only period.

Known limits

  • The package does not provide the nert study’s end-to-end pipeline, automatic ASReml-like experimental-design recognition, or a generally validated production solution for arbitrary complex METs. Factor-analytic GxE remains outside the admitted surface.
  • Concurrent INLA work is memory-intensive. One three-worker stress run ended in an INLA segmentation fault and was recovered as a typed worker failure. Not every worker count is known to be safe.
  • The nert release-shaped smoke test found a structurally aliased variety-type parameterisation. flexyBayes selection already refuses an unidentified protected design and records unavailable candidate columns. Choosing among variety identity, type and within-type contrasts remains an estimand decision for the study, not an automatic formula rewrite by this package.

flexyBayes 0.12.1

A containment release. An INLA fit whose hyperparameter lies outside the bound of a stated prior is refused by name, the capability record the package installs is generated from the live registry, and the README and known issues state what each engine fits at the level the evidence supports. No model family, penalty family, engine or exported function is added.

Breaking changes

  • INLA refuses a fit outside the bound of a stated prior (prior_support_violated). After every INLA fit, on the per-row route and both aggregated routes, each hyperparameter under a uniform bound is checked on the scale INLA fitted: its mode and its 2.5% and 97.5% quantiles must lie inside the bound INLA received, within 0.1% of the standard deviation. The refusal names the parameter, its standard deviation at the mode, the interval, the bound, the INLA version and the route. backend = "auto" falls back to brms, as for any INLA failure. On a Poisson design with a random term aliased with a fixed factor, 0.12.0 under INLA 26.08.07 returned 45 of 100 repeated fits with a standard deviation near 1,400 against a bound of 3, and 0.12.1 fitted 72 of 100 inside the bound and refused 28. Under INLA 25.10.19 all 100 fitted inside. Every INLA fit records the check in fit$extras$support_audit (known issue 17). This corrects the 0.12.0 statement that a stated bound binds on INLA.

    The check also refuses a fit whose mode is inside the bound when INLA’s reported interval reaches past it. A uniform prior cuts the posterior off at the bound, so such an interval misstates the posterior. This happens on a weakly identified component with few levels: on agridat::john.alpha with random = ~ rep + rep:block, the default bound on rep (three levels) is 3.05 and INLA’s interval runs from 0.17 to 3.65, so the default INLA fit is refused, in 8 of 8 repeats. A half-normal prior on the standard deviations fits the same model on INLA, and brms fits it under the default.

  • na_action = "augment" on brms refuses a missing Student-t response by name (brms_cannot_augment_nongaussian). 0.12.0 admitted the family and stopped with an untyped emitter error. Augmentation on brms is admitted for the gaussian and lognormal families, and the lognormal route is now checked by a live fit against the complete-case posterior.

Claims and evidence

  • The README, known issues and ?flexybayes state what each engine fits. INLA fits nested and multi-stratum random effects, a per-environment residual and the baseline heteroscedastic MET model (iid genotype, iid genotype-by-environment and a sectioned residual), checked on small simulated trials. Unstructured genotype-by-environment covariance fits on brms only, and factor-analytic covariance on INLA is experimental. The capability row formerly called the full MET model carries the baseline name.

  • The installed capability record is generated from the registry. inst/validation/execution_grid/capability_matrix.csv is written by the same generator as the README and known-issues tables, and an installed- package test compares each shipped row with the live registry. The grid outcome files come from this release’s grid run on its tarball.

  • Known issues 16 and 17 name their measured causes. Issue 16, an INLA program crash on a Poisson response with three non-zero counts, is refused as inla_program_failed and is not a regression: the grid cell’s data changed when the grid fixture’s random-number state moved. A half-normal prior with scale 1.53 fits the same data. Issue 17 is the aliased-term design above.

  • The high-missingness warning reads a disagreement between engines as weak identification. The 30% threshold is described as a rule of thumb.

  • API_STABILITY.md pins to the 0.12.x line.

  • The default variance prior is unchanged in this release. It stays the uniform bound on each standard deviation, on both engines. No execution-grid cell that fitted in 0.12.0 is refused by the check, but the john.alpha design above, the data of a validated ASReml comparison, is. The release plan therefore moves the default to a half-normal prior on both engines in 0.13.0. Tests that fit john.alpha as rep + rep:block on INLA, and two with a weakly identified component, now state a half-normal prior or a wider bound.

flexyBayes 0.12.0

The model a fit reports is the model it ran. Gaussian models on INLA are fitted per row on a standardised response, default priors follow the units of the response and of each covariate, offsets fit on both engines, a stated bound on a standard deviation binds (corrected in 0.12.1: INLA can still return a mode outside the bound, and 0.12.1 refuses such a fit), and every fit records which prior reached which engine slot as the engine reports it back. No model family, penalty family, engine or exported function is added.

Breaking changes

  • Gaussian models are fitted per row. The aggregated Gaussian route combined the within-cell sums of squares with a fixed gamma prior on the residual precision, so the residual prior a caller stated, or the package’s default, was not the prior fitted, while prior_summary() reported it: aggregated fits with residual bounds of 0.05 and 50 returned the same residual standard deviation. aggregate = "auto" now fits a Gaussian model per row. aggregate = TRUE on a Gaussian model, and flexybayes_stream() on a Gaussian family, refuse with aggregation_residual_prior_not_composed before any fit or chunk is read. flexybayes_stream(fit = FALSE) still returns the Gaussian sufficient statistics, and binomial and Poisson models still aggregate. The 0.10.0 release carries the same construction: an aggregated Gaussian fit made with 0.10.0 should be refitted per row.

  • Aggregated and streamed fits report no marginal likelihood. On the aggregated representation the engine’s value omits constants that depend on the data, and under standardisation it scales with the number of cells. summary() reports the value as not available and names the reason (aggregated_evidence_unavailable).

  • Estimated correlation matrices are fitted on brms only. us(f):g and the correlated random slope (x | g) refuse on INLA with correlated_covariance_requires_brms, and backend = "auto" routes both to brms. On INLA each was one field under a joint Wishart prior, which ties the variances to the correlations: us(env):gen on agridat::besag.met returned a genetic correlation of 0.142 where ASReml returns 0.930.

  • A response containing NaN or an infinite value refuses with response_not_finite, naming the rows. INLA fitted such a model without a message, and brms stopped with an error that named neither the row nor the value. NA is still a missing response, handled by na_action. On flexybayes_stream() a missing count refuses too (aggregation_response_incomplete), as aggregate = TRUE already did: the cell holding it used to drop out of the fit without a message.

  • INLA refuses a heterogeneous residual on a count family, as brms does (heterogeneous_residual_family_has_no_sigma). residual = ~ dsum(~ units | f) on a Poisson or binomial model split the response into one likelihood per section, which is the unsectioned model, and fitted it without a message.

The fitted model is the written model

  • Gaussian models on INLA run on a standardised response. Every Gaussian identity-link fit on INLA is fitted to (y - m) / s, with m the mean of the response when the model has an intercept and s its standard deviation. Fixed and random effects, hyperparameters, fitted values and the linear predictor with their marginals, the marginal likelihood, DIC, WAIC, CPO, PO and the draws are mapped back exactly, and stated priors are restated on the standardised scale in closed form. The same model on a response recorded in different units used to return different variance components without failing. Checked across random-effect structures and response multipliers from 0.01 to 1000.

  • Default priors on INLA follow the units of the data. An unstated random-effect standard deviation takes the bounded default prior. It used to take INLA’s log-gamma precision prior, and on a design with a four-level random intercept a call stating only the residual prior returned a block standard deviation near 1e7 in 20 of 20 fits. The default bound on an uncorrelated slope’s standard deviation is divided by the standard deviation of its covariate, and the default fixed-effect prior is scaled by each numeric column’s standard deviation: on lme4::sleepstudy with Days multiplied by 0.001, 1 or 1000, the Days coefficient is 10.467285959588 at every scale, 7.8e-12 from lme4. Stated priors are never rescaled, and every filled default is recorded on the fit and printed by prior_summary().

  • The default bound reads a transformed response. The bounded default on the residual and group standard deviations is five standard deviations of the response. It was read from a column named like the response, so log(y) and I(10 * y) took a bound of 1 on both engines whatever the units. It is now five standard deviations of the modelled response, after any offset, on both engines.

  • A tight uniform bound binds on INLA (corrected in 0.12.1: the start is inside the bound, but the returned mode can still leave it, as known issue 17 records). INLA starts its search at a standard deviation of 0.135 for a random effect. A stated uniform bound below that started the search outside the bound, where the prior is flat, and the search never entered it: sd(group = "geno") ~ uniform(0, 0.05) on a Poisson model returned 0.61. The search now starts inside the bound whenever INLA’s own starting point lies outside it, and the same fit returns 0.05. Every other fit is sent to INLA as before. When INLA fails on a model that states a uniform bound, the refusal says so and names two remedies.

  • Offsets in the fixed formula fit on both engines. offset(z) used to be dropped without a message: Reaction ~ Days + offset(Days) on lme4::sleepstudy returned the coefficient of the model without the offset (10.47 against lme4’s 9.47). brms receives the offset in its formula and INLA through inla()’s offset argument, and on the standardised Gaussian response the centre, scale and default priors read y - o. On Poisson, offset(log(E)) is the same model as exposure = "E". predict() evaluates the offset on the fit data or on newdata, and a newdata missing an offset column refuses (newdata_offset_missing). A binomial offset on the aggregated route, projection selection with an offset, a non-finite or wrongly sized offset (fixed_offset_invalid) and an offset in the random or residual formula refuse by name. INLA agrees with lme4 on sleepstudy to 1e-11.

  • Every fit carries a model manifest at fit$extras$manifest: every stated or default prior with its source and the number of engine slots that used it; every engine slot with the prior sent and the prior the engine reports after fitting (INLA’s all.hyper, brms’s prior_summary()); the route; and whether the marginal likelihood is available. prior_summary() prints from it, including each input no slot used and the reason. A stated sd() prior on one factor of a multi-way interaction, such as "a" on a:b:cc, refuses with prior_target_not_in_model. It used to be accepted without reaching the fit. A stated prior on the interaction itself, sd(group = "a:b:cc"), is accepted on INLA.

  • fitted() and residuals() work on aggregated count fits, and include the random effects. Both used to stop with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”, and the fitted values stored on the fit were the fixed part alone, off by up to 3.49 counts on a Poisson test design. Row-level fitted values now come from INLA’s cell fitted values mapped to each row and multiplied by that row’s exposure or trials and exp(offset). They match a per-row fit to within 1e-6. A streamed fit keeps a head sample of its rows, and where that is shorter than the data, fitted(), residuals(), model.matrix() and the emmeans and insight data hooks refuse with streamed_rows_not_retained, and update() with update_streamed_fit_not_supported. nobs(), glance()$nobs and summary()$n_design report the same integer. augment() on INLA, the log-density producer, and predict() and marginaleffects predictions on a non-identity link now refuse with registered reason codes.

  • ranef() on INLA reports the levels the user wrote for every random-effect index the INLA formula builder generates. Estimates, standard errors and intervals are unchanged.

Selection

  • Each fold learns its own preprocessing. In fb_select() the penalised reference model’s centring, scaling and prior are learned on each fold’s analysis rows. Out-of-fold comparisons are gated on a declared score contract at each model stage (reference_predictive and decision_predictive on the certificate), the certificate records how hyperparameters were treated and how the selection data were reused, and a projection metric other than elpd refuses before any fit (projection_metric_unsupported). projpred’s own k-fold search refits the reference model on the whole sample, and the certificate names that approximation.

  • A base model’s offset is subtracted in the fold substrate every provider shares.

Smaller fixes

  • fb_gblup_cv(seed = ) puts the caller’s random-number state back when it returns.
  • The warning on predict(classify = ) given newdata names the argument brms accepts for new levels, allow_new_levels = TRUE.
  • Package code reads list fields by exact name where $ partial matching used to supply them: the preflight’s term label and level count, the plan’s cell estimate and the selection bridge’s response convention. A multi-way fixed term without a label now gets one label, x:z.
  • fb_select() has an example.
  • On INLA, the warnings that the variance-component table could not be built, or that a hyperparameter lost its row, no longer say the fit is unaffected. Either can follow from a mode outside a stated prior bound, and both now say to read fit$inla$summary.hyperpar against the bounds (known issue 17).

Documentation

  • The explanation of why shrinkage priors are not fitted on INLA is corrected wherever it ships. Given one local scale per coefficient, a Laplace, horseshoe or R2D2 prior is Gaussian. The model then carries a hyperparameter for every coefficient, more than INLA’s integration is built for. The capability tables mark those rows n/a on INLA, because fb_select() fits them on brms.
  • The scaling benchmark (inst/validation/benchmark_scaling.md) is measured on a Poisson model: peak memory of 712 MB at ten million rows and 734 MB at five billion, streamed from disk. The earlier Gaussian measurements are kept as a dated record.
  • API_STABILITY.md records triangulate() as internal and the flexybayes_stream() change. inst/KNOWN_ISSUES.md records the bound change under issue 8 and lists the problems open for 0.13.0 as issues 10 to 16.

Refusals

The registry holds 204 codes, 187 at 0.11.0. New in this release: aggregation_residual_prior_not_composed, aggregated_evidence_unavailable, correlated_covariance_requires_brms, fixed_offset_unsupported, fixed_offset_invalid, newdata_offset_missing, projection_metric_unsupported, prior_family_has_no_residual_scale, prior_vc_sd_superseded_by_prior, evidence_not_computed, response_not_finite, streamed_rows_not_retained, update_streamed_fit_not_supported, augment_not_available_inla, log_density_producer_unavailable, predict_link_not_supported and marginaleffects_link_not_supported.

flexyBayes 0.11.0

fb_select() becomes a Bayesian verb. It fits a reference model in which a declared block of candidate fixed effects carries a joint shrinkage prior and the covariance structure is integrated over, not plugged in. It selects a parsimonious submodel by projection predictive inference where the reference model’s structure permits it, and refuses by name where it does not. On request, it triangulates the result against an external penalised optimiser on the same folds. It does not claim that posterior summaries are numerically identical to glmnet, and there is no configuration under which a penalised mode is reported under a Bayesian label.

Breaking changes

  • fb_select()’s signature has four axes instead of one engine argument. workflow, provider, prior and decision are recorded independently on every result, so a penalised-likelihood mode cannot be described as a posterior. covariance, metric, alpha, lambda, stability and sensitivity leave the public signature. The metric is set in fb_decision(). Path and stability quantities belong to the optimiser workflow and are returned only when it ran. metric and covariance are still accepted for one release with a deprecation notice.

  • The certificate’s covariance estimand is read from the fold object, not from an argument. The public argument defaulted to plugin_mean_covariance while the folds worked in reml_plugin_covariance, so a certificate could describe a computation that had not happened. Every field naming an estimand, a provider, a convention or a route is now copied from the object that produced it. The regression test injects a disagreement and requires the certificate to follow the fold.

  • Five penalty families are withdrawn from the public grammar. group_lasso, exclusive_lasso, sparse_group_lasso, group_exclusive and adaptive have no provider in this release (sparsegl, grpreg and an internal proximal solver are not shipped). Naming one refuses with selection_penalty_family_withdrawn. Their component traits remain in the resolver, and their return is a later phase with its own gates.

New

  • fb_penalty() declares the joint shrinkage prior: target ~ family(...) formulas resolved in written order against the model matrix’s own assignment map, never by string matching on names. Five families are available, ridge(scale), laplace(scale), elastic_net(lambda, alpha), regularized_horseshoe(p0, ...) and r2d2(mean_R2, prec_R2, cons_D2), plus none() to exempt coordinates from shrinkage. Targets are term(everything()), term(x1, x2), term(c("x1", "x2")) and term(matches("^SLGA_")). The tidyselect vocabulary is not supported.

    ridge, laplace and elastic_net target the candidate block exactly: the first two through coefficient-specific prior rows, the third through a target += contribution over the candidate indices carried in stanvars. regularized_horseshoe and r2d2 are class-wide: brms refuses a coefficient-specific row beside a class-wide special prior, so a base carrying protected fixed effects beyond the intercept refuses with penalty_block_targeting_unsupported and the refusal names both ways forward: an exactly-targetable family, or scope = "all_fixed", an explicit opt-in under which the protected coefficients also sit under the global-local prior and the certificate records protected_under_global_shrinkage.

  • fb_resamples() becomes public unchanged: folds on original units before any transformation, frozen factor levels, and an assessment fold carrying a level the training fold never saw is refused, not dropped.

  • fb_decision() declares how the answer is read off: the method (projection, full, posterior_threshold), the metric, the rule (one_se, min, tolerance) and the search. It validates at construction, so a tolerance rule with no tolerance, or a posterior threshold with no practical effect size, refuses before anything is fitted.

    A posterior threshold is a decision rule and is labelled one everywhere it appears. A continuous shrinkage prior puts no posterior mass at zero, so the quantity it thresholds is not an inclusion probability.

  • penalty = NULL has a provider. Under workflow = "bayes" it refits the base’s own engine (INLA or brms, whichever fitted the base) inside every assessment fold and scores held-out clusters from posterior predictive draws. This is the Bayesian no-penalty reference and the baseline for every shrinkage family.
