On INLA the assessment rows enter the refit with an NA response and their held-out grouping levels relabelled, so for a level the training rows never saw the predictive is marginal over the random effect.

  • benchmark = TRUE runs the closed-form generalised-least-squares arm and, where a penalty was given, the glmnet arm on the same folds, the same prediction target and the same candidate design. The generalised-least-squares arm is workflow = "unpenalized_benchmark", provider = "gls_reml_plugin", and is never labelled Bayesian. It can also be asked for on its own.

  • fallback = "none" is the default. A Bayesian request whose provider is absent refuses with selection_provider_absent or selection_fallback_not_authorised, naming the package and the install line. fallback = "glmnet" is a deliberate choice, fires only on an absent provider and never after a failure. When it fires, the workflow becomes penalized_optimizer, the object prints the substitution on its first line, and the certificate records fallback_fired = TRUE.

  • fb_select(plan = TRUE) reports the resolved axes, the compiled prior blocks and their route, the projection structure gate and a cost estimate without fitting anything. The per-fit figure is the base model’s own recorded wall time, labelled as a floor.

  • lgm_gate() gains a twelfth structural check. A joint shrinkage prior on a model routed at INLA refuses with prior_family_unsupported_inla. A Laplace, horseshoe or R2D2 prior is Gaussian given one local scale per coefficient, so the model can be written as a latent Gaussian model. It then carries a hyperparameter for every coefficient, and INLA’s integration is built for a few. No public call reaches the check, because fb_select() fits every shrinkage prior on brms (see “An INLA-fitted base can carry a shrinkage prior” below). The capability matrix carries one row per family with inla = "n/a" and brms = "fits", each anchored on the generated-code assertions.

  • Accessors: print(), tidy(), glance(), augment() and plot(type = c("elpd_by_size", "rank_stability", "shrinkage", "benchmark")).

  • The projection search runs on clustered draws: 20 clusters for the search and 100 for the predictive evaluation. Projecting a multilevel submodel is a fit per draw, so projecting every draw at every search step inside every fold does not finish on a problem of the size this module is for. Both settings travel on the result and on the certificate, so a reader can see what the elpd column was computed from.

Every comparison declares what it does and does not claim

Three equivalence levels, and every stored comparison carries exactly one.

  • map_exact_fixed_covariance: the posterior mode under fixed covariance and fixed residual scale is the minimiser of a named penalised objective, and a numerical oracle gates the claim.
  • posterior_predictive_comparable: the provider expresses the family, but the covariance is integrated or the residual scale is free, so the estimands differ and only predictive risk on common folds compares.
  • no_identity_expected: the provider has no representation of the family at all. The arms are reported side by side and nothing is claimed.

A Bayesian arm always integrates the covariance and leaves the residual scale free, so a glmnet benchmark beside it is posterior_predictive_comparable for ridge, laplace and elastic net, and no_identity_expected for the regularised horseshoe and R2D2. The words “same as glmnet” appear nowhere unqualified.

The glmnet conventions are measured, not recalled

Under glmnet 5.0 on this machine, with standardize = FALSE, intercept = FALSE and a convergence threshold of 1e-16, the map from the canonical objective 0.5 ||z - A beta||^2 + pen(beta) to glmnet’s own lambda was measured against two references independent of glmnet, the ridge closed form and the canonical KKT residual.

  • The L1 part maps as lambda_canonical / n, with KKT residual 9.8e-09.
  • The L2 part does not. glmnet measures its ridge penalty against a response scale, and that scale is the uncentred root mean square, not either standard deviation. lambda_canonical * rms(y) / n recovers the closed form to a maximum absolute coefficient deviation of 1.3e-10. Leaving the response scale out gives 1.9e-02, the population standard deviation 7.4e-03 and the sample standard deviation 7.2e-03.

The convention is measured at run time by .fb_sel_glmnet_convention(), stored on the provider certificate as provider_lambda_convention, and pinned by a test. A change in glmnet’s convention fails that test instead of moving the answer silently.

Projection refuses two structures it was measured against

projpred 2.10.0’s reference-model constructor was exercised cell by cell. Two structures the package fits are refused, and the refusal names the feature:

  • (x || g), the uncorrelated random slope. get_refmodel() rejects the spelling. The two-term form (1 | g) + (0 + x | g) is accepted, and the refusal says so.
  • (1 | gr(g, cov = K)), the known-covariance term vm() and ped() lower to. get_refmodel() rejects a function call on the right-hand side of a group term. The alternative the refusal names is decision = "full", which keeps the shrinkage posterior with no selection.

us() and fa() translations and heterogeneous residual structures have no executed gate, so they refuse with projection_structure_unsupported too. Turning any of those rows green requires a test that runs it.

Adequacy is a gate, not a note

Before any decision runs, the reference model must pass two checks. The tri-state convergence contract reads divergences, treedepth saturation, E-BFMI and bulk and tail effective sample size. A fail refuses with penalty_sampler_diagnostics_failed. An unverified verdict is carried on the certificate and printed, and is not treated as a pass. A posterior predictive check on the observed mean and standard deviation must place both inside (0.005, 0.995), else penalty_reference_model_inadequate. A projection inherits the reference model’s misfit.

For the regularised horseshoe the count of coefficients whose shrinkage factor falls below one half is reported against p0, labelled orthogonal_design_kappa_approx: the scalar formula holds for a standardised near-orthogonal design, and a correlated candidate block does not have one shrinkage factor per coefficient at all.

Three silent wrong answers closed

Found by the 2026-09-12 audit of this release’s own selection work. Each one fired on the formulas the module exists to serve, not on an edge case.

  • tidy() marked a chosen factor or interaction as dropped. Retention was matched by design-column name against a chosen set written in formula terms, so a projection that kept f and x1:f reported fB, fC, x1:fB and x1:fC as not retained. The column map now carries the term each column came from, every decision records the vocabulary its chosen set is written in, and retention is read in that vocabulary: terms for the projection, full and an optimiser support, and coefficients for the posterior threshold, the one decision that chooses column by column. tidy() gains a source_term column.

  • A mismatched scoring-unit key silently became row numbers. When the unit key and the provider’s pointwise log predictive densities named different numbers of observations, the aggregation replaced the key with row numbers and carried on. The cluster-level standard error then became the row-level one, too small by roughly the square root of the cluster size, on the clustered models a unit was declared for. It now refuses with selection_scoring_unit_mismatch, naming both lengths.

  • search = "L1" was stored and passed to the provider. It reached projpred::cv_varsel() beside a search_terms block built for a forward search, and no gate had run that combination and read the ranking back, so whether the forced protected and random terms survive an L1 path is unmeasured. fb_decision(search = "L1") now refuses at construction with projection_search_unsupported. The forward search is the search this release executes.

The structure gate leads, and it chooses the decision

Projection predictive inference is the right Bayesian decision given a reference posterior, and it is available for a minority of what this package fits. The gate that says so was executed and accurate, and it was reported after the fact.

  • fb_decision()’s default method is "auto". It resolves to "projection" where every structural feature of the reference model has an executed projection gate behind it, and to "full" (the reference posterior under the shrinkage prior, with no selection) where one does not. The resolution and the gate verdict that produced it are recorded on the result and on its certificate. A known-covariance genomic or pedigree base used to refuse only after a reference model had been sampled. It now gets shrinkage without a selection, and says why.

  • Naming "projection" explicitly on a red gate refuses before the reference model is sampled, with the feature that failed. The gate inside the projection also stays. It reads the reference model, not the base, and can still refuse a base whose gate was green.

  • fb_plan() and print.fb_select() lead with the structure-gate table: one row per structural feature the model carries, its verdict, and the run behind that verdict.

  • The clustered-draw counts are on the first print line of a projection result and in ?fb_select: the search runs on 20 clustered draws and the predictive evaluation on 100. Projecting a multilevel submodel is a fit per draw.

  • The capability matrix says what each family can be asked for. The regularised horseshoe and R2D2 rows say that exact block targeting holds only when the base’s fixed part is intercept-only, and name the two ways forward otherwise. The known-covariance genomic and pedigree row says shrinkage yes, projection no. The selection vignette carries the same table, keeps its intercept-only base with the sentence that says why, and adds a base with a protected covariate under laplace().

  • The withdrawn families are not offered a schedule. The refusal names what was removed and what is available. It no longer says when the group, exclusive and adaptive families return, because no dated decision stands behind that. The release record above is the only place the withdrawal is described, and the resolver keeps their component traits.

glmnet is a check that cannot be misread

posterior_predictive_comparable says the arms were scored “on the same folds, target, loss, unit and candidate design”. The Bayesian penalised route wrote no out-of-fold score at all (it set aggregated = NULL), so the label was printed about a comparison that had not been made.

  • The penalised Bayesian route writes the same unit-level out-of-fold table the penalty = NULL route writes: elpd, rmse and nlpd per resampling unit, under the requested prediction target, on the folds the projection used. It reuses the per-fold machinery for the reference model. It costs one reference refit per fold per model, so it runs under benchmark = TRUE and the certificate says which of the two situations a reader is in.

  • The certificate splits the glmnet role in two. mode_oracle carries the Tier-1 claim and is populated only from an arm that solved the canonical objective with the covariance plugged in and the residual scale held fixed, and whose comparison against the primary answer was made under the same two conditions. It is therefore empty on every sampled route, and says why. predictive_side_by_side carries the out-of-fold comparison and is written only when the arms really do share one loss, at one unit, on one set of folds. An arm that aggregated at a different number of units is dropped and named, not averaged in.

  • posterior_predictive_comparable needs the shared table stated. The gate defaults to closed: a caller who has not built the table cannot reach the level by forgetting. Horseshoe and R2D2 against glmnet stay no_identity_expected whatever the table, because glmnet has no representation of a scale mixture at all.

  • The glmnet benchmark arm is scored at the resampling unit. It scored at the fold, so a side-by-side table would have put a twelve-site standard error beside a two-fold one and called them one loss.

An INLA-fitted base can carry a shrinkage prior

fb_select() fits the reference model through brms whatever fitted the base. The parsed model is engine-independent, and the reference is a re-emission of it with an extended fixed part and the base’s own priors carried through the brms prior translation. lgm_gate()’s twelfth check nevertheless ran on the BASE’s intermediate representation whenever the base was INLA, so a user with an INLA fit asking for a Laplace prior was told the prior was impossible on INLA, about a fit that was never going to INLA.

The check no longer runs on the base. An INLA-fitted base with a joint shrinkage prior samples on brms. The certificate records reference_engine = "brms", the print method and the plan say the base was fitted by a different engine, and the certificate carries reference_fitted_on_brms among its approximations. No public call reaches the check: fb_select() is the only verb that takes a shrinkage prior, and it always fits on brms. The check stays as an internal guard.

The prior is calibrated against the information that is there

  • calibration_n counts resampling units, not rows. The Piironen and Vehtari calibration of a global-local prior reads tau0 = (p0 / (p - p0)) * sigma / sqrt(n), and the elastic net’s canonical objective carries n in front of its penalty. Both were given the row count. In a clustered design that overstates the information about a coefficient by roughly the cluster size (a hundred plots in ten sites are not a hundred independent pieces of evidence about a site-level covariate), so the global scale came out too small and the prior over-shrank. The number is now the count of resampling units where one was declared, and the row count where none was. The certificate carries the basis and the row count beside it, and the object prints the calibration wherever the two differ.

    brms derives the horseshoe’s global scale from par_ratio and the number of fitted rows and offers no way to set it otherwise. Measured against brms::make_standata(), hs_scale_global = par_ratio / sqrt(N) exactly. The calibration is therefore moved by moving par_ratio, and the certificate carries the canonical p0 / (p - p0) beside the ratio brms was handed so a reader can see the second is the first re-expressed.

  • A class-wide family refuses an unstandardised candidate column. The reference model is a re-emission of the formula, not a design-matrix fit, so a factor contrast or an interaction product has no data column to centre and divide and is left on its own scale. brms puts ONE global-local prior on the whole population-level vector, so a 0/1 dummy then sits under the same local scale as a numeric already at unit standard deviation and the shrinkage applied is a property of the contrast coding. regularized_horseshoe and r2d2 now refuse with penalty_candidate_columns_unscaled, naming the columns and the two ways out. ridge, laplace and elastic_net state a scale per coefficient and keep the candidate_columns_not_standardised approximation they already carried.

  • The mode-identity language carries its conditions everywhere. A ridge or Laplace prior’s mode equals the corresponding penalised objective only with the covariance plugged in and the residual scale held fixed. The Bayesian route integrates the covariance and samples sigma, so no arm of it reaches map_exact_fixed_covariance. The identity belongs to the fixed-covariance, fixed-sigma substrate the exact-limit bridges test, and ?fb_penalty and ?fb_select say so.

The correlated random slope on INLA is demoted to an analogue

A validation run against ASReml 4.2.0.392 and lme4 found that (x | g) on INLA carries the defect the us(f):g row was demoted for, on a second route, through the iid2d field instead of iidKd.

On lme4::sleepstudy the slope variance comes back at 46.37 at the posterior mode (52.10 at the mean, 50.19 at the median), against 35.076 in ASReml and 35.072 in lme4. That is 32 per cent high at the mode, which is the summary a REML estimate is comparable to, while the intercept variance on the same fit is 7 per cent high and the residual 0.4 per cent. Rescaling the response by ten is an exact transformation under which a correlation is invariant, and it moves the reported intercept-slope correlation from 0.02 to 0.969 while REML holds at 0.066. The ratio of the intercept standard deviation to the residual doubles on the same transformation. The numerical-confirm gate does not separate the two: the unscaled fit reports mode status 0 and passes it on every call, and the rescaled fit passes it on some calls and not others: five identical tenfold calls returned mode status 0, 0, 0, 2 and 6. The one protection a user has here therefore stays quiet on the fit that is wrong.

The row is reclassified from covariance-family to analogue in the translation registry, with the measurement recorded in the row. The change propagates to inst/TRANSLATION.md, the shipped CSV, and, through the capability matrix, to README.md and inst/KNOWN_ISSUES.md, where it is open issue 2 beside the us() row.

fb_select() refuses a base that carries the term on INLA (selection_base_not_allowlisted), because the selection substrate whitens by the base’s own covariance and a block that is a third too large would set the rotation every score is read through. The refusal quotes the measurement and names the brms route, which the comparison did not exercise and which writes (x | g) natively. A brms base carrying the term stays admitted, and a test asserts that it does.

The scale-invariance check in tests/testthat/test-metamorphic-scale-invariance.R gains the sibling tripwire. It asserts the ratio of the slope standard deviation to the residual, not the correlation: across three identical unscaled fits the ratio reproduces to the third digit while the correlation spans 0.048, and a metamorphic gate is only as reproducible as the component it reads. As with us(), the tripwire fails when the defect goes away and its message names the records to close. The cause is not established and is shared between the two routes, so a repair has to cover both.

ranef() on an INLA fit reports the levels the user wrote

.fb_random_inla() restored a level label only where INLA returned the ID column as CHARACTER, which is what a plain ~ g produces because INLA is handed the factor itself. Every structured term is indexed by an integer column the emitter builds, so ID came back as 1 ... n and the guard never fired: rep:block on agridat::john.alpha reported levels "1" to "18" where ASReml reports rep_R1:block_B1 ..., and (Days | Subject) on lme4::sleepstudy reported "1" to "36" with the subject identifiers sitting unused on the fit.

Two of the four BLUP comparisons in the September validation programme could not be made at all. Aligning by row order was not attempted: interaction() orders rep fastest and ASReml orders it slowest, so a positional match would have been silently wrong on exactly the row where it looked easiest.

Levels now come from the grouping factor itself, composed in the order the emitter’s index uses and in the user’s own labels, not the legalised ones. An interaction group reports the interaction level, R1:B1, with the separator its group name already uses.

The correlated random slope also returned two list elements under one name, because both of its index names mapped to the single label <x> | <g>, and ranef(fit)[["Days | Subject"]] reached one of the two blocks with nothing to say which. The two blocks are now named for what they hold, (Intercept) | <g> and <x> | <g>, and each reports the group’s own levels over its own half of the iid2d field instead of the whole field twice.

Documentation

  • ?fb_engine documents adapt_delta. The help page listed the recognised options as n_samples, warmup and chains while the constructor had accepted a fourth since the start of this release. It is the option that clears a selection run refused with penalty_sampler_diagnostics_failed, and both selection runs in the September validation programme hit that refusal, so a reader following the documentation would have concluded the refusal could not be cleared. The page now carries a “Recognised options” section giving all four, brms’s own 0.8 default, the reference fit’s 0.95, and the run that needed 0.999.

Refusals

The registry moves from 163 codes to 184. selection_penalty_not_implemented is withdrawn, because the penalty is implemented and nothing throws it any more. New in this release: selection_penalty_spec_malformed, selection_penalty_target_unsupported, selection_penalty_target_not_in_model, selection_penalty_target_ambiguous, selection_penalty_family_unknown, selection_penalty_family_withdrawn, penalty_hyperparameter_invalid, penalty_block_overlap, penalty_block_targeting_unsupported, penalty_factor_contrast_ambiguous, penalty_scaling_column_constant, penalty_sampler_diagnostics_failed, penalty_reference_model_inadequate, penalty_runtime_budget_exceeded, projection_structure_unsupported, projection_family_unsupported, selection_provider_absent, selection_fallback_not_authorised, selection_prox_mode_not_converged, selection_penalty_blocks_not_expressible, prior_family_unsupported_inla and selection_decision_invalid. Each is registered beside the site that throws it and each is fired by a test.

The audit close adds three more, taking the registry to 187: selection_scoring_unit_mismatch, projection_search_unsupported and penalty_candidate_columns_unscaled.

Dependencies

Suggests gains projpred and glmnet. Nothing moves to Imports, the package loads and checks with neither installed, and every provider-requiring test is gated on the provider being present.

flexyBayes 0.10.0.9000 (development version)

  • us(f):g on INLA is no longer described as covariance-family equivalent to ASReml’s, because it is not. Paired against ASReml 4.2.0.392 on agridat::besag.met, the route returns a genetic correlation of 0.142 where ASReml returns 0.930, and 0.198 / 0.231 / 0.320 against 0.898 / 0.915 / 0.955 over three environments, with genotype variances four to five times larger while the residual variance agrees closely. The gap reproduces across refits (three runs spanned 0.141 to 0.147 over two environments), so the answer is stably wrong, not noisy. A stable wrong answer is harder to notice, and a repeatability screen rates it as fine. The gap is the finding. The third digit belongs to one run, and the banked fixture carries it.

    It also fails a check that needs no external reference. Multiplying the response by ten is an exact transformation under which a correlation is invariant, so it must not decide whether the model fits. Here it does. Across eight identical rescaled calls none converged, and the correlation returned spanned -0.894 to +0.686, nearly its whole range, against an unscaled value reproducible to 0.1448-0.1474. ASReml returns 0.930 at every scale.

    The rescaled fit at least says so, through a non-zero mode status and a failed numerical confirm. The unscaled fit, which is the one a user runs and the wrong one, reports mode status 0 and passes its confirm. The gate fires on the fit nobody would trust and stays quiet on the one they would.

    The translation registry row is classified analogue, no longer covariance-family. The capability matrix says which route to read the correlations from, and inst/KNOWN_ISSUES.md carries the measurement as the package’s largest open correctness gap. The cause is not established. The joint Wishart the iidKd field carries has a plausible mechanism, its scale being set from the response variance, but the emitted hyper block has not been read directly. A hypothesis about this exact route was published once and withdrawn for that reason. Reproduce with oracle scenarios 06_us_dim2 and 07_us_dim3.

  • A named argument written twice is refused (grammar_argument_duplicated). The 0.10.0.9000 grammar contract validated the set of named arguments a special form answers to and never their multiplicity, which left the audited defect class alive in two shapes. vm(g, V = G, V = G) was accepted and lowered to a single vm term, and which copy survived depended on how the parser indexes. s(x, k = 5, k = 9) reached mgcv’s own argument matcher and raised “formal argument ‘k’ matched by multiple actual arguments”, a base error about package internals and the untyped escape the contract exists to close. Both refuse before dispatch, for closed name sets (vm, ped) and for the open-ended s() set alike.

  • A b() prior target that is not one coefficient name is refused (prior_target_not_a_single_name). The target was read with as.character() on the unevaluated argument, which deparses a call head-first. b(c("x", "z")) became the three coefficient names c("c", "x", "z"), with a phantom c nobody wrote, and b(starts_with("x")) became c("starts_with", "x"). Neither was refused. The length-three target passed through fb_prior() and fb_plan() intact and failed inside the emitter with “the condition has length > 1”, an R internals message raised about a formula the user had written. The two documented spellings, b("treatment") and b(treatment), are unchanged. Vector and tidy-select targets need a typed term resolver, not a coercion. Until there is one, the refusal says so.

  • The system-memory probe shells out once per session instead of once per plan. fb_plan() resolved a memory ceiling on every call, and each resolution spawned a child process, measured at about 9 ms. Total system RAM does not change while an R process runs, so the answer is cached for the session, including when the probe is unavailable. The native probes also check that the executable exists with Sys.which() before spawning it, and a Solaris host without kstat no longer reaches the optional helper that would call it. A child’s stderr cannot be redirected from inside R once it is running, so the only defence is not to spawn it.

  • A converged INLA fit could be the wrong converged fit, and the package finds the better one and returns it. Fitting random = ~ diag(env):gen to agridat::besag.met returned no genetic variance in any of six environments on nineteen of twenty-four runs of the identical call, and substantial variance on the other five. Every one of the twenty-four reported Mode status: 0 and Numerical confirm: PASS, because the optimiser had converged, to a solution with every component pinned at zero. ASReml 4.2 on the same rows returns 5.84 and 5.45 in two of those environments, stably.

    The cause is not a prior this package chose. The emitted INLA formula was read directly and carries the intended prior. Tightening it from uniform(0, 192.6) through uniform(0, 40) to uniform(0, 10), and then to a penalised-complexity prior, did not remove the collapse. That separates this case from the factor-analytic specific variance and the iid2d Wishart, which were both the package’s own defaults.

    When a component comes back pinned at zero, the fit is restarted from a mode where that component carries real variance, and the two marginal likelihoods are compared. On besag.met the restart was better by 65 to 154 log units, so the restarted fit is the one returned. The numerical gate is re-run against the fit actually returned. The adoption is stated in the convergence block and as a message, so the user does not have to infer it from a number that moved. A fit with nothing pinned at zero never enters the probe and costs nothing.

    After adoption, five identical calls return every component substantially non-zero. They agree with ASReml closely where a component is well identified (5.76 to 7.77 against 5.84, 6.03 to 7.96 against 5.45) and sit above it where ASReml has pinned the component at the boundary. That last difference is the documented one between a REML estimate, which can sit exactly at zero, and the mean of a posterior over a non-negative parameter, which cannot.

  • Variance components of a diag() term reported the wrong prior. summary(fit)$varcomp$prior read engine default on every sd_<group>__<level> row while the emitted formula carried the package default, or the user’s own prior, verbatim. The heterogeneous routes emit one field per level keyed by the inner group, so the canonical row names never matched the prior spec’s key, and every one of them fell through to the closing branch.

    The cost was not cosmetic. Reading that column was how the first pass of the ASReml oracle suite concluded that the prior layer did not reach diag() at all. That finding was written up before the emitted formula was read, and withdrawn once it was.

  • An ASReml oracle suite, and the repeatability screen that runs first. data-raw/asreml_oracle/ carries a specification written before any comparison ran, a scenario matrix pairing ASReml 4.2 against the built flexyBayes tarball on byte-identical public data, and a screen that asks whether a structure returns the same answer twice before any comparison is attempted. Tolerances are fixed in the specification, and the exit gate admits no outcome in which a tolerance moves.

    The screen found five of ten structures unstable before the mode-adoption fix, with the factor-analytic row swinging by a factor of fifteen between identical calls. It also found its own blind spot. Its first criterion returned STABLE for the structure already measured as bistable, because all three runs had collapsed alike and a consistently wrong answer scored as a repeatable one.

  • A malformed dsum() fitted a homogeneous residual instead of refusing, and it was one of four ways the parser let a malformed formula through. dsum(~ units | env) asks for one residual variance per section. Written without the bar, as dsum(~units), the parser returned a plain units residual. The fitted model is a plausible neighbour of the one requested, so it converges, prints credible output, and agrees across both engines, because both engines consume the same parsed representation.

    An external translation audit reported this and one other case, fa(env) without a rank raising a base subscript error. A fuzz corpus over all 22 special forms (129 malformed variants) found the class was wider than both. 15 cases raised an untyped base error across five forms, 7 lowered dsum() to units, 15 zero-argument forms parsed into a term whose variable was NA, and 32 calls had a surplus argument discarded without comment.

    Each branch of the parser read the arguments it expected without checking what it was given. The argument shape of every special form is declared once, in R/grammar_contract.R, and checked once, before the parser dispatches. Across the same 129 cases, untyped errors fall from 15 to 0 and 55 silent acceptances become typed refusals, while every well-formed call parses into the term it always produced. Eight reason codes join the registry: grammar_arity_too_few, grammar_arity_too_many, grammar_named_argument_unknown, grammar_argument_empty, dsum_malformed, fa_rank_missing, pol_degree_invalid and multivariate_smooth_unsupported. fa()’s rank and pol()’s degree must be whole numbers written into the formula. Previously as.integer() turned TRUE, 1.5 and "1" each into a rank of 1.

  • A negative factor-analytic loading was printed as a collapsed variance. The collapsed note in summary(fit)$varcomp flagged any component that was not a correlation and not sigma whose upper credible bound sat below 1% of the residual scale. Factor-analytic loadings are signed. A crossover interaction gives a negative loading, which is a result and not a failure, and its negative upper bound satisfies that inequality for arithmetic reasons, so it was labelled as a variance pinned at zero. The shipped FA(1) and FA(2) summaries both carried one.

    The note applies only to components the canonical namer marks as non-negative scales, the rule the fit-time collapse warning has always used. The two surfaces had disagreed. A component the namer does not produce is left unflagged and is not put through a test written for standard deviations.

  • What each ASReml structure is lowered to, and what grounds the claim, is written down. “ASReml syntax” covered lowerings of three different kinds without saying which was which: exact structural translations, covariance-family equivalents whose identification and priors are not ASReml’s, and one analogue built from a different basis. inst/TRANSLATION.md and inst/translation/translation_registry.csv carry one row per structure with its syntax vintage, its translation class, its precondition where it has one, and the independent oracle that grounds it. Both are generated from a single table and pinned by a staleness test.

    Three consequences are visible to readers. spl() is an analogue of ASReml’s spline, not a translation of it, and says so on every surface. The basis, the scaling and the prediction rule differ, and no equivalence has been established. Residual-side at() and ped() are labelled as the ASReml 3 spellings they are, since ASReml 4 replaced them with dsum() and vm() and may reject them. A fit carrying a factor-analytic term no longer reports Representation: exact. The loadings are anchored to one at a level taken from factor-level order, which spans the factor-analytic family only where the leading loading block supports the anchoring, so the line names the condition.

    Several rows record none at this anchor in the oracle column. The banked ASReml comparisons were taken at 0.10.0’s predecessors, before this line added or changed the INLA factor-analytic, us(), correlated-slope, sectioned-residual and combined multi-environment paths.

  • Four claim surfaces had drifted apart, and are held to each other by tests. The package help said eight vignettes ship and cran-comments said eleven, where four ship. The help and the startup banner still offered triangulate() as the signature feature after it was unexported, and two @seealso entries pointed at fb_structured_cov(), withdrawn at 0.10.0. vpredict() was exported but absent from both the pkgdown reference index and API_STABILITY.md. Each is corrected, and each is held by a test that fails when the surfaces disagree.

  • Five documented examples generated random data without a seed. The invariant checker had marked seed discipline present because it found set.seed() calls somewhere in the sources. Each @examples block is linted on its own and must seed itself before its first draw.

  • The ASReml reference recipe no longer carries a workstation path. data-raw/asreml_reference.R set .libPaths() to an absolute path under a home directory, which made the recipe unrunnable by anyone else. It reads FLEXYBAYES_ASREML_LIB instead. A test scans every source directory for absolute home paths, not only the four the estate-level pre-commit rule reads.

  • The unstructured and correlated-slope covariances get a Wishart scaled to the data, which removes an instability the package had blamed on INLA. iid2d and iidKd carry one joint Wishart on theta1, and its scale matrix defaults to the identity, a prior centred on unit variances. There is no standard-deviation slot to translate a DSL prior into, so the default was left unspliced, and that unit-scale prior stayed in force on data of any scale.

    On lme4::sleepstudy, whose response has a standard deviation near 50, eight identical calls to (Days | Subject) returned intercept standard deviations from 0.50 to 54.8 and correlations from -1.00 to +0.75, with marginal likelihoods 31 units apart, and none near lme4’s REML answer of 24.7. That was recorded here and in the capability table as a property of INLA’s iid2d parameterisation. It was the package’s own default.

    The scale matrix is taken from the response’s own variance, the same basis the uniform-SD default already uses. The slope block is scaled by the response variance per unit of the slope variable, the scale a slope lives on. R is on the variance scale, established by fitting the candidates. Five identical calls return intercept SDs of 25.7 to 26.9 against 24.7, slope SDs of 6.7 to 7.2 against 5.92, correlations of -0.07 to +0.15 around 0.066, and sigma 25.66 to 25.81 against 25.59. The correlation’s run-to-run spread falls from 1.95 to 0.22.

    The earlier note said to fit such designs on brms. That advice is withdrawn.

  • vpredict() on INLA drew its variance components from the integration grid, not from the posterior. The generic draws path uses INLA::inla.posterior.sample(), which resamples the configurations INLA assembled the fit from. Those are coherent, with each latent draw paired with the hyperparameters it was drawn under. The hyperparameters themselves take only as many distinct values as the grid has points. On a 24-genotype alpha design, 1000 draws carried 15 unique values. A heritability built on them had a posterior supported on 15 atoms while its quantiles were reported as a smooth interval, and its minimum was its 2.5th percentile.

    vpredict() draws from the fitted joint hyperparameter posterior via INLA::inla.hyperpar.sample(), whose columns carry the same names the canonical map already keys on. The point estimate barely moves (0.633 to 0.638 on that fit). The tails do: the interval widens from [0.460, 0.800] to [0.426, 0.816], and the support exceeds it. A test asserts that more than half the draws are distinct and that the range is wider than the central interval, which a 15-atom distribution cannot be.

  • The refusal a user reads is four lines, not sixteen. The R Journal review of 0.10.0 quoted one back. It carried a per-rule diagnostic string, four lines explaining what backend = "auto" already does, an unconditional sentence about a roadmap item for mixtures (printed whether or not the model contained one), a two-argument override incantation, and a second header above the one the printed refusal already had. It carries the rule ids, the reasons, and one route onward, with ?lgm_gate for the rest. Measured on the same model: 1225 characters to 531.

  • README rebuilt to what a reader needs. It was 371 lines, of which 178 were commented-out prose, and it carried claims the code had overtaken. fa(env, k):gen was still listed as “refused (no active engine)” in two places. It is 147 lines: what the package does, how to install it, one worked example with its printed output and an lme4 cross-check, the generated capability table, and where to report problems. The separate “Supported ASReml syntax” and “Model types” sections are consolidated into the one generated table plus a syntax vignette, as the review asked.

  • The vignette deck is four pages, not eight tutorials. Mixed models in brief, Bayesian estimation in brief, the ASReml syntax covered and not covered, and one worked illustration replace 2696 lines of tutorial. The previous deck is kept under vignettes-reserve/, excluded from the build and not deleted, and every one of its published URLs redirects to the page that covers the same ground.

  • The illustration is fitted both ways, on two public trials. The ASReml side was computed once with a licensed ASReml 4.2.0.392 by data-raw/asreml_reference.R and stored, so the page builds without a licence and every number attributed to ASReml has one source.

    On the whole john.alpha alpha design the two agree: heritability 0.636 against 0.640, intervals almost coincident. Degrade the same trial and they part. At twelve genotypes ASReml’s delta-method interval runs from -0.533. At six, it runs from -1.256 to 1.256, wider than the parameter space. Two random-deletion designs put the upper bound above 1. The posterior intervals stay inside [0, 1] throughout, because every draw does.

    On the dasilva.maize multi-environment trial both engines fit fa(env, 1):gen with a dsum residual and agree on the residual and specific variances. The genetic correlations do not agree. ASReml’s delta-method intervals reach 1.034 and 1.342 for two correlations, which cannot exceed one. The same quantities are exact posteriors here, from one vpredict() line, and stay in range.

    Two claims are recorded as not demonstrated. Carrying a lost plot as a design row, instead of deleting it, changes the variance components hardly at all under deletion at random (the ignorability result). The factor-analytic fit does not fail on a design with whole genotype-by-environment cells removed, which an earlier note in this project predicted it would.

  • A failed brms fit no longer blames the model for a broken compiler. The brms path compiles a Stan program, and a missing or mismatched C++ toolchain reaches R as a downstream symptom, invalid connection, while the compiler’s own message goes to the console. Reported verbatim, that sends the reader looking for a fault in their model. On a failed fit the toolchain is checked directly by compiling a three-line C++ program. Only if that fails does the message name the toolchain, give the check and the repair, and note that backend = "inla" compiles nothing. A machine that compiles fine gets the engine’s own words unchanged.

  • vpredict(): exact posterior functionals of the variance components. ASReml’s vpredict() returns a heritability with a delta-method standard error, which linearises at the REML estimate and does not know where the parameter space ends. That is how an ASReml heritability acquires an interval running below zero. This one transforms the draws, so the interval is a quantile interval of the functional’s own posterior and cannot leave the range the function maps into.

    vpredict(fit, h2 ~ sd_gen^2 / (sd_gen^2 + sigma^2))

    It reads canonical draws, not engine-native ones, so the same call gives the same answer on either engine. It agrees with lme4’s REML variance components put through the same ratio. A functional naming a component the fit does not carry refuses and lists the ones it does. It does not resolve the name against the caller’s workspace.

  • The correlated random slope fits on both engines: (x | g). It used to refuse at ingest, before any engine was chosen, on the ground that no active backend represented the structure. It is the uncorrelated slope with the correlation freed: one intercept SD, one slope SD, and the correlation between them. Both engines fit it. INLA holds all three in a single iid2d field over an index blocked intercepts-then-slopes, with the slope block entering as a fixed-scaling copy of that same field weighted by x. brms writes (x | g) verbatim.

    On simulated data with an intercept SD of 1.2, a slope SD of 0.6 and a correlation of 0.60, INLA returns 1.11, 0.66 and 0.569 with the residual at 0.338 against 0.35, and agrees with lme4::lmer()’s REML fit of the same model on all three. A crossover fixture with a correlation of -0.7 comes back negative with an interval excluding zero. Components are reported as sd_<g>, sd_<x>_<g> and cor_<g>__Intercept__<x>.

    Where the design separates the intercept from the slope weakly, INLA’s mode for this structure is not unique, and the capability table says so. On lme4::sleepstudy, with 18 subjects, five identical calls return intercept standard deviations between 0.5 and 4.6 against lme4’s 24.7, and correlations spanning -0.96 to +0.99. Each reports mode.status = 0, INLA’s own convergence flag, and each has a different marginal likelihood. Hand-written INLA, with this package not loaded, reproduces the same spread, so it is a property of the iid2d parameterisation and not of the translation. INLA’s own restart machinery fires on some of those runs (inla.core.safe: rerun with improved initial values, from the safe argument that defaults to TRUE), so the engine detects a suspect solution without the answer settling. The boundary-collapse warning fires on these fits. Fit such designs on brms, and refit before reporting a correlation.

  • The prior column reports the prior that reached the fit. us(f):g and (x | g) are iidKd fields on INLA, and their hyperparameters are a single joint Wishart. theta1 carries it, and every later theta reports prior = "none". There is no standard-deviation slot. The package’s own default was therefore never spliced in, which is correct, but summary() and prior_summary() went on reporting it as though it had been. Those components read engine default, and prior_summary()$not_applied names them with the reason. An explicit prior on these groups still refuses by name and is not dropped.

  • The factor-analytic covariance fits on INLA: fa(f, k):g. This is ASReml’s flagship multi-environment-trial model, and the one this package had declared no engine could fit. INLA has no latent model called “factor analytic”, which is what the refusal said, and it does not need one. Each common factor is a single latent field entered once per level of f as a scaled copy, and copy=’s scaling parameter is the loading, so the loadings arrive with a posterior, which REML cannot give.

    Factor j is anchored at level j and entered from that level onward, the zero upper triangle ASReml uses to identify the loading matrix against rotation. An anchored loading is therefore absent from the summary, not reported as an estimate of 1.

    On simulated data with four environments and loadings 1.6, 0.5 and -0.9, the fit returns 1.598, 0.505 and -0.846, with the common-factor SD at 0.890 against 0.9 and the residual at 0.309 against 0.30. A crossover environment comes back negative, not merely small. fa(f, 2) recovers both loading columns on five environments.

    The prior is the package’s contribution here, and it has a test. On INLA’s default log-gamma precision, the specific variance at the level carrying the largest loading collapsed to 0.007 against a truth of 0.25. .fb_default_prior_targets() had no branch for this term, because the term had never been reachable. With the package’s own standard-deviation prior wired in, it recovers to 0.165 with an interval covering the truth, and a test asserts that no specific variance collapses.

    The dispatch-wide refusal that claimed “INLA’s f() has no factor-analytic latent model” is gone. brms’s own emit refuses the term by name, so a per-engine limit sits in that engine’s emit, not in a rule that speaks for both.

  • Unstructured genotype-by-environment covariance fits on INLA: us(f):g. INLA holds the whole k-by-k covariance as one iidKd field over a blocked index. Standard deviations of 0.8, 1.2 and 0.5 come back as 0.768, 1.256 and 0.447 with the residual at 0.354 against 0.35. Components are reported as sd_<g>__<f><level> and cor_<g>__<f>I__<f>J, the names brms uses for (0 + f | g).

    The correlations are shrunk toward each other by INLA’s Wishart hyperprior: a true 0.7 / 0.2 / 0.4 returns near 0.71 / 0.41 / 0.61. That is a property of the prior, measured and documented, not a translation defect. The test asserts what is defensible, not three point values.

    An explicit standard-deviation prior on this term refuses. INLA’s iidKd hyperparameters are prec1..preck and cor12.. under a joint Wishart, with no slot for a scalar SD prior. Splicing one in makes INLA drop it silently. The package’s auto-default is left unspliced, so INLA’s Wishart governs, and an explicit prior is refused by name, not discarded.

    us() beyond five levels refuses and names fa(f, k):g instead. INLA’s iidkd is a different parameterisation above that width, and k(k+1)/2 parameters is the problem the factor-analytic structure exists to solve.

  • devtools::check() spends less time in tests. Eight test blocks that compile a Stan program carry skip_on_cran(), cutting the check-path test phase from about six minutes to under three. The gating is per block, not per file. The six files involved hold 69 test blocks and only 11 brms fits, so gating whole files would have dropped roughly sixty cheap tests out of check(). devtools::test() still runs everything.

  • The full multi-environment-trial model fits on INLA: a sectioned residual dsum(~ units | f), alone and together with an interaction random effect. The refusal claimed that “INLA folds residual variance into the likelihood and has no separate residual-structure surface”. The multiple-likelihood interface is that surface: a matrix response with one Gaussian family per section carries one observation precision each. The claim was the package’s, not INLA’s, and this is the second of ASReml’s two MET workhorses.

    Per-section residual standard deviations of 0.25, 0.80 and 1.60 come back as 0.246, 0.748 and 1.722. With an interaction random effect added (the combination that was unreachable on INLA because both halves refused), the fit recovers the genotype (0.913 against 0.9), the genotype-by-environment (0.534 against 0.5) and all three residuals.

    Sections are reported as sigma_<level> on the standard-deviation scale, the vocabulary the brms path already used, so dsum() reads the same on both engines. The matrix response is built inside the INLA call only. fb$response stays a scalar name and data is untouched, so every consumer that reads the response as a vector is unaffected.

    at(f, level):units conditions the residual on selected levels and does not ask for one variance per level. That is a different model and refuses.

  • Heterogeneous variance by factor level fits on INLA: diag(f):g, idh(f):g, at(f):g. One free standard deviation per level of the outer factor and no covariance between levels. This is one of ASReml’s two multi-environment-trial workhorses, and it was refused on INLA with nothing but an allowlist behind the refusal.

    INLA writes it as k independent iid fields, one per level, each on an index that is NA outside its level. On simulated data with per-environment standard deviations of 0.4, 1.0 and 2.0 the fit returns 0.48, 1.08 and 1.95 against lme4’s REML values of 0.46, 1.05 and 1.89, with the residual at 0.293 against 0.292.

    The component is reported as sd_<g>__<f><level>, which is what brms calls the same quantity, so diag() reads identically on both engines.

    at(f, level), which conditions the effect on selected levels instead of asking for a heterogeneous variance across all of them, is a different model and still refuses.

  • Uncorrelated random slopes (x || g) and factor-by-numeric interactions y ~ f * x fit on INLA. Both were refused at run time unless an on-disk artefact recorded that a “three-arbitrator” comparison had passed. One of those arbitrators was an engine withdrawn at 0.9.3, so the criterion could not be re-run and the refusal became permanent, blocking a working capability.

    The runtime gate is retired. The agreement it stood in for is checked in the suite, where every other capability claim in this package lives: against lme4’s REML fit for the random slope, and against lm() for the fixed interaction. Both references are independent of this package’s parser and emit.

    Retiring the gate exposed a defect it had been hiding. The uncorrelated slope emit wrote f(<g>_for_slope_<x>, ...) into the INLA formula and never created that index column, so the fit would have failed with object not found. Because the gate refused the class before the emit ran, the path was never exercised end to end and the defect could not surface. It is fixed, and the column refuses by name if it would overwrite a user column.

    Component labels no longer leak the generated index name. The slope reports as sd_<x>_<g>, the name its prior is registered under.

  • Nested and multi-stratum random effects fit on INLA: ~ rep:block, ~ env:rep:block. These refused, with a message asserting that INLA’s f() machinery could not represent the term class without an SPDE or kronecker expansion. That was not true. The term is an iid field over the interaction index, which is also what brms’s (1 | a:b) means, and the alpha-design in the report that raised it (agridat::john.alpha) fits in seconds.

    The two engines and lme4’s REML fit of the same model agree: residual 0.293 against 0.286, sd_gen 0.397 against 0.378, sd_rep:block 0.288 against 0.265. Only observed cells get a level, as in lme4 and brms.

    The generated index is named after the interacting factors and never reaches a user-facing label. The summary reports sd_rep:block, the name brms uses, so the same component lines up across engines. A generated index that would overwrite an existing column refuses by name, so the field is never indexed by whatever that column holds.

  • A transformed response fits: log(yield) ~ env. The left-hand side was required to name a column, so every peer’s ordinary spelling (lm, lme4, brms and ASReml all evaluate it) was refused with “Response variable not found in data” (reported as issue #14). The left-hand side is evaluated against the data when it does not name a column.

    The refusal was the visible half. The quiet half was worse. Several consumers read data[[fb$response]] behind a guard that returned early when the name was absent, so a transformed response reported no missing responses on data that had them, and skipped the binomial response check and the aggregation route’s missing-data branch. Those reads go through one resolver.

    The expression is evaluated with baseenv() as its enclosure, so base transforms resolve and an object in the user’s workspace does not. A mistyped column still refuses and does not bind to a global of the right length.

    Streaming aggregation reads named columns from disk and cannot evaluate an expression, so it refuses one by name (stream_response_must_be_a_column) instead of asking the reader for a column that does not exist.

  • Units followed through time: random = ~ ar1(t):g. The grouped temporal field (AR1 along t within each level of g, independent across levels, three hyperparameters shared by every level) is a named capability with its own matrix row, anchor test and execution-grid cell. The commuted spelling g:ar1(t) (ASReml’s usual order for a set of plots followed over seasons) parses to the same field instead of falling to an untyped interaction that refused. The model line, the field block and the note naming the ASReml residual used to describe this field as ar1(t):ar1(g) with four parameters. They describe it as what it is. This is the units-by-occasions covariance of Verbyla and Cullis (1992) written on the random side.

flexyBayes 0.10.0

The first release prepared for CRAN. Its criteria are held as a runnable contract in the development repository. The checks that read source answer immediately. The ones that need a build, a check run or a person are listed as unmet until their artefact exists, and the contract exits non-zero while any of them is outstanding. That file is not shipped in the tarball.

Breaking changes

  • The declared validation tier is V2, not V3. 0.9.2 declared V3 and waived four of its validation floors. 0.9.3 shipped declaring V3 with that waiver already expired, and it is not re-issued. V2 is what the registered evidence supports. The four floors are recorded in inst/validation/README.md as the next validation arc, and a second consecutive waiver on the same floors is the pattern a waiver exists to prevent.

  • Eleven functions are withdrawn from the public API, taking the export count from 44 to 33. The extreme-value and Dirichlet maximum-likelihood fitters (fb_gev(), fb_family_gev(), rgev(), fb_dirichlet(), fb_family_dirichlet(), rdirichlet()), the EMMAX genome-wide association pair (fb_gwas(), triangulate_gwas()), and the three exports that abstained unconditionally (fb_met_summary(), fb_log_posterior(), fb_structured_cov()) are no longer exported. They remain in the package, documented as internal and covered by their existing tests, and their S3 print and tidy methods stay registered so the objects still print.

    The package returns a Bayesian posterior where REML returns a point estimate. Four of the withdrawn fitters are maximum-likelihood or frequentist, none of them has a cell in the execution grid, and together they were a quarter of the public surface sitting outside the package’s own execution oracle. fb_structured_cov() joined them late. No active engine emits an fa() term, so its only reachable outcome is a message and an empty list, the same ground the other two abstainers were withdrawn on. fb_gblup_cv(), genomic_summary() and triangulate_genomic() were considered for the same treatment and kept. The first is taught and executed in the multi-environment-trials and genomics vignette, and the other two operate on posterior draws.

  • effectsize is no longer listed as a supported downstream package. It was named in the DESCRIPTION Description, in Suggests, in README.md, and in two vignettes. One of those vignettes also said a flexybayes-class method dispatched through parameters::model_parameters(), which was never true. It is removed from all five. The standardised-effect section of the downstream-analysis vignette keeps its worked example, which needs nothing but the draws.

  • coda moves from Imports to Suggests, and splines leaves Imports altogether. The only trace of coda in R/ was a roxygen @importFrom tag, and neither effectiveSize() nor gelman.diag() was called there. The test suite does use it, so it moves to Suggests. splines was the same defect one release later: importFrom(splines, bs) with bs() called nowhere in R/. It moves to Suggests, where the one test that calls splines::bs() needs it.

Diagnostics

  • A variance component pinned at the boundary warns, on any term type on the per-row emit paths. The existing detector covered one case, sd_spatial running to its floor against the nugget. Any other component could reach the same state reporting only a note = "collapsed" cell in summary(fit)$varcomp, which is easy to read past, while the convergence block reported a converged mode. Both engines raise a warning naming the component, its upper credible bound and the residual scale, with three routes out. Silence it with options(flexyBayes.silence_boundary_collapse_warning = TRUE).

    The threshold is 0.01 of the residual SD, calibrated against a measured floor. A sweep of 112 INLA fits with the group SD set to exactly zero, crossing n in {30, 60, 120, 240, 480} with 5, 10 and 20 groups, puts the upper credible bound of a genuinely null component at 0.0228 of the residual SD at the lowest. The ratio is flat in both n and the group count, because it is a floor set by the prior. The degenerate mode sits two orders of magnitude below that: 2.5e-04 on the besag.met fit this was built from. The threshold sits in the gap. It is the constant the varcomp table already used to mark a row collapsed, so the warning and the table agree.

    It has two structural limits. It compares against a residual SD, so it reads Gaussian-scale fits and is silent on families carrying no sigma row. It needs credible bounds, so it covers the per-row emit paths only. The aggregated streaming emitters record variance components as posterior means with no quantiles, so there is no upper bound to read.

  • na_action documentation separates the identity from the arithmetic. Under ignorability the posterior is the same whether a missing cell is augmented or omitted. That is a statement about the posterior and not a promise about what an optimiser returns. The two settings hand the engine an intact design and a ragged one, and on a weakly identified mode they can land in different places. augment remains the default and the recommendation. The caveat stands wherever the identity is stated, README.md and the brms emit path included.

  • Every export carries a runnable \examples{} block. Nine had none. Five of the new blocks are wrapped in \donttest{} and guarded on the engine, so they do not fire where it is absent. The three tidier re-exports (augment, glance, tidy) document their generics on man/reexports.Rd, which carries no example. Their methods do.

  • Config/testthat/parallel is false. It was true, and the parallel runner stalls: workers spawn, orphan, and sit at 0 per cent CPU indefinitely once the suite reaches the brms and INLA tests. Every release run so far had forced sequential execution from the outside, and TESTTHAT_PARALLEL=false does not reliably prevent the workers from spawning. The setting hung the suite for anyone who runs devtools::test(), so it is fixed in the package.

Documentation

  • The vignette deck is rebuilt: eleven pages become eight, and 8,591 lines become 1,651. The structure follows the grouping the co-authors approved, and the standing brief with it: concise, grounded in open-source data, “reproducibility and insightful commentary over exhaustive coverage”. The old deck had inverted that last line.

    The merges: the formula surface absorbs dispatch and refusals, because the grammar and the machinery that turns a term away are one subject. Regression and hierarchical models become one foundational page. Summaries, model comparison and triangulation become one “after the fit” page. Nothing was dropped. Old article URLs redirect.

    Every page opens with a panel giving the problem, the ASReml line, the flexyBayes line, what the posterior adds and what it costs, so a reader can tell from the first screen whether the page is the one they want. Every capability and refusal table is generated from the package’s own capability record, so a table cannot drift from the code.

  • The unsupported structures are listed in one place. They were scattered across five points of the old formula vignette with no list. The formula page carries two generated tables: structures neither engine represents, and structures one engine fits and the other refuses.

  • Section headings are sized correctly. html_vignette sets body text at 14px and h1 at 35px, because h1 is meant to be the document title. Every numbered section in the deck was an h1, so sections rendered at two and a half times the body and competed with the title, and inline code in a heading landed near 30px. The shared header include sets a normal document hierarchy and sizes code in a heading against its heading.

  • The spline section of the spatial vignette runs. It was an unevaluated block with data = ... as a literal stand-in. It could not be executed, produced no output, and read as though it worked. It fits the composite on stroup.nin and reports the result. The splines collapse because the autoregressive field is already carrying the gradient, and the boundary warning flags this so it is not read as a zero trend.

Corrections to the package’s own claims

Each of these was a statement the code did not support. Each is recorded here as a fix, and each has a guard that fails the lint workflow if it recurs.

  • The package-level help said twelve vignettes ship, including one on arriving from an ASReml call. Eleven ship, and that page was folded into the getting-started vignette at 0.9.3.

  • API_STABILITY.md said every public export carries a lifecycle::badge("experimental"). None did. The document states the lifecycle stage without claiming a badge.

  • README.md described the release as “a stable release of the supported capability set” six lines above a block stating that every export is experimental.

  • CITATION.cff carried a date-released eight days earlier than the tree it described.

  • An internal flag word reached a shipped surface in inst/validation/README.md.

  • cran-comments.md, SECURITY.md, SUPPORT.md and .zenodo.json all still named 0.9.3. The coherence test that exists to catch this could not. Its “superseded version” pattern was written as 0\.[0-8]\. and so was blind to the 0.9.x line at the moment the tree reached 0.10.0. It compares parsed versions and needs no edit at the next bump.

  • Withdrawing eleven functions left their \examples{} blocks calling them by bare name, and R CMD check runs the examples of internal help pages too. Ten pages were affected. They reach the functions through the namespace, and a new guard fails when any example calls something the package does not export.

  • The boundary-collapse threshold shipped in this release at 0.05 of the residual SD on the strength of a single simulation, with a claim that a null component returns an upper bound near 0.43 of the residual SD. The package’s own suite falsified it: seven fixtures whose components are null by construction warned. The claim is withdrawn and the threshold re-grounded on the sweep described above.

  • The release contract reported its machine-evidence criteria as skipped and exited zero regardless, so the suite, both check runs, the grid, lint, pkgdown, the clean room and CI could each be red while it reported success. Those criteria are unmet until evidenced, and the full tier exits non-zero while one is outstanding. The criterion asserting that a boundary-pinned component warns was satisfied by the existence of its test file. It runs the tests.

  • inst/KNOWN_ISSUES.md item 7 still said the INLA-crash re-route to brms was silent and that “what is ours to fix is the silence around it”. The re-route emits a one-shot message and the fit’s class records the engine, so the silence had already been fixed and the note had not followed. This file ships in the tarball and the startup message points at it, so the stale text was user-facing. An earlier pass recorded this same finding as not reproducing, on a search for “silent” and “fallback” against a document that says “silence” and “falls back”. That rejection was wrong and is corrected in the release record.

  • API_STABILITY.md advertised output_file, format and allow_new_levels on the two predict() methods. None is a formal of either, and ... swallowed them. output_file belongs to fb_plan() and allow_new_levels to the classify path. The paragraph naming the methods had been corrected once already without its argument list being checked.

  • The guard asserting that every declared import is used counted mentions in comments and the package name inside message strings, which is how splines stayed in Imports unused. It requires an imported symbol to be called.

  • fb_plan()’s own documentation showed fb_plan(fixed = ...), which errors. The fixed part is the first argument, formula, and fixed fell into .... The guard that checks documented arguments against formals() skips any function taking ..., so nothing could see it.

  • The ignorability caveat was missing from ?flexybayes, the most-read of the four places the identity is stated. The guard that exists to prevent this read a hand-written list of files, and the list was missing the entry point. It derives the surface set, and its patterns tolerate the words a writer puts between “posterior” and “is the same”. A literal phrase match had been reading past the entry point’s wording even once the file was in scope.

  • README.md pointed at ?na_action, which is not a help page. The argument is documented on ?flexybayes.

  • API_STABILITY.md described fb_from_brms() and fb_from_asreml() as wrapping a fitted object. They parse a formula and return the internal representation. Passing a brmsfit fails.

  • API_STABILITY.md still said glance() refuses on an INLA fit in its interoperability section, having been corrected in its own 0.8.x table in this same release, so the same claim appeared twice in one file. It also documented predict.flexybayes(), removed at 0.9.3, and omitted fb_complete_grid(), genomic_summary() and ranef() from what presents itself as the export inventory. A new guard fails when an export is not named there.

  • “There is no silent fallback” appeared on three surfaces while backend = "auto" does re-route to brms when the INLA program fails. The re-route is reported by a message, so it is not silent, but the sentence read as a promise that auto never changes engine. All three name the numerical-fallback path. The routing message itself asserted “this is a multi-stratum designed experiment” for every gate refusal it handled, which is false for most of them. It names the refusal reason instead.

  • inst/validation/scenarios.yaml shipped inside the tarball declaring tier: V3 and 0.9.3, the tier this release steps down from. It is in the version-coherence gate with the other metadata surfaces.

  • The boundary-collapse floor was asserted in prose and restated as a literal in its own test, so a wrong threshold that still sat below the literal would have passed. The 112-fit sweep is recorded at inst/validation/boundary_calibration.csv, regenerable through tools/calibrate_boundary_collapse.R, and the test reads the floor from it. Restoring the original 0.05 threshold fails three tests.

  • The guard asserting that every advertised structure spelling is executed read the grid source, which declares cells, not the record of what ran. It reads the code column of the recorded run.

flexyBayes 0.9.3

This is the first public release of the 0.9 line. Versions 0.9.0 to 0.9.2 were staged locally and never published. Their sections below stand as the record of what changed between 0.8.3 and this release.

Breaking changes

  • The third native fitting engine, quarantined since 0.9.0, is withdrawn from the package entirely. No code path, export, S3 method, backend registry row, refusal code, worker script or Suggests entry for it remains. fb_greta(), fb_from_greta() and gretaR_status() are removed, and a call to any of them fails with “could not find function” instead of a typed refusal. 0.9.2 was the last version whose code could read draws from an object fitted by that engine. Re-entry, should it ever be proposed, is a fresh implementation, not a repair of retained code. greta and tensorflow leave Suggests.
  • backend = "greta", backend = "gretaR", or any other unrecognised backend name raises an ordinary unknown_backend refusal naming the two active engines, "inla" and "brms", before match.arg() could report a less specific error.
  • fb_backend_status() reports the two active engines only (INLA, brms). The rows for the withdrawn engine and its dormant sibling are gone, with the Python/TensorFlow discovery probe that populated them.
  • The refusal-code registry drops eleven codes and adds nine (116 in 0.9.2, 114 now). Removed: backend_quarantined, the six codes of the dormant sibling engine’s refusal family, the two codes naming the withdrawn engine directly, low_rank_requires_greta (renamed, below) and the stale predict_kernel_invalid_include, which had no live raise site. Added: unknown_backend, low_rank_smooth_unsupported, cell_count_exceeds_integer, inla_program_failed, weights_requires_gaussian, weights_not_aggregatable, binomial_response_not_binary, update_unnamed_argument_not_supported and at_field_per_level_hyper_not_representable. fb_refusals() gives the authoritative list.
  • fb_met_summary() abstains unconditionally (met_summary_not_ available). Its breeder summaries were derived from the withdrawn engine’s realised factor-analytic effects, and neither active engine emits an fa(env, k):gen term. summary() and, on a diag() or us() covariance, brms::VarCorr() remain the way to read a multi-environment trial’s genotype-by-environment structure.
  • fb_log_posterior() abstains unconditionally (fb_c4_unavailable): neither active engine exposes an equivalent producer.
  • update() refuses the unnamed-formula idiom by name (update_unnamed_argument_not_supported). update(fit, . ~ . + z) previously discarded the formula silently and re-fitted the unchanged model. Named arguments (fixed =, random =, residual =) are unaffected.
  • GBLUP and pedigree-BLUP cross-engine comparison is two-engine (INLA, brms). triangulate_genomic() and genomic_summary() keep their shape.
  • The unreachable streaming predict(..., output_file = ) path is removed. The engine-specific predict() methods had shadowed it since before this release.

New features

  • A per-trial separable spatial field. random = ~ at(trial):ar1(row):ar1(col) fits one AR1 x AR1 field per level of trial on INLA, sharing the row correlation, column correlation and field variance across levels (INLA replicate), with the complete-lattice check run per level. brms has no lowering for it, as for the single-field spelling. A level-conditioned at() on this spelling refuses by name (at_field_per_level_hyper_not_representable).
  • weights = is lowered for the Gaussian family (identity link) in the precision sense Var(y_i) = sigma^2 / w_i on both engines: INLA’s per-observation scale, and on brms a known offset on the sigma distributional parameter that reproduces the same precision-weighted likelihood (brms’s own weights() addition term is a likelihood-power quantity and was not used). Both engines match lme4::lmer(weights = ) closely. Doubling every weight leaves the fixed effects unchanged and doubles the fitted residual variance. Any other family, a non-identity Gaussian link, or aggregate = TRUE with weights refuses by name (weights_requires_gaussian, weights_not_aggregatable).
  • fb_plan() accepts the ASReml fixed / random / residual grammar, auto-detected as flexybayes() does. Before, random and residual were silently dropped, so the plan could name a backend for a fixed-effects-only reading of the model. print.fb_plan() and print.fb_aggregation_plan() print the row count, cell count, rows per cell and a plain verdict on whether aggregation will pay, with the threshold stated.
  • A non-syntactic factor level (a level containing a space) no longer kills the INLA emit untyped: levels are legalised inside the emit and the user’s own labels are printed back by summary(), coef(), ranef(), predict(classify = ) and confint(). backend = "auto" now routes such models to INLA where it fell through to brms. Purely numeric levels are left alone.
  • glance() returns its one-row summary on INLA and aggregated fits as it did on brms fits, with sampler-specific columns NA.
  • A family = "binomial" response outside {0, 1} refuses before any engine runs (binomial_response_not_binary), naming the column, the offending values and the remedy, on all three routes.
  • fb_plan(), backend_decision() and validate_approximation() carry runnable examples.

Bug fixes

  • An INLA engine death surfaces as a typed refusal (inla_program_failed) naming the design size, the largest design this package has verified an INLA per-row fit to complete, the binding random-effect term and the remedies, instead of a raw engine message after tens of minutes.
  • The aggregation planner’s cell count is carried as a double. Past R’s integer limit the plan records cell_count_exceeds_integer instead of an NA count: aggregate = "auto" takes the per-row route and says why, aggregate = TRUE refuses by name. A grep gate keeps the cast class closed.
  • A streamed fit’s print() banner names its engine and route instead of (unknown engine).
  • Gate labels spell GxE in ASCII. A gate message that named a pre-renumber vignette filename is corrected, and a test requires every vignette filename named in R/ to exist.
  • triangulate()’s transform_b is exercised at a non-NULL value.
  • The low_rank_smooth refusal is renamed low_rank_smooth_unsupported and says what is true: no active engine consumes a rank-truncated smooth basis.

Documentation

  • The tutorial deck is eleven contiguous pages. The page From an ASReml call is removed. Its accessor tour (variance components, random effects, predicted means, observation counts, missing plots, the empirical variogram) lives in Getting started, section 6, with no asreml() call anywhere in the deck. Pages 06 to 11 and 16 are renumbered 05 to 11. The pkgdown site redirects every old address.
  • Every figure carries a caption and a reading sentence. html_ vignette leaves captions off by default, so a fig.cap reached the page only as alt text. Every page sets fig_caption: true.
  • Every page is copy-paste runnable: library(flexyBayes) is the first visible line, seeds are visible, and no code depends on a hidden chunk. Streaming exact aggregation runs end to end on temporary .fst files (single file, shards, fit = FALSE inspection, binomial with trials =, poisson with exposure =), states how the Gaussian case stays exact as the emit implements it, and cites its methods.
  • Getting started lists the four verbs one per row. The formula surface shows weights = fitting on Gaussian and refusing elsewhere. Spatio-temporal models shows the per-trial field. The kinship comment in Multi-environment trials attributes the marker-count normalisation to Astle and Balding (2009), which is what the code does.
  • @param random separates terms that parse and fit from terms that parse and refuse by name (fa() on both engines). README carries a short paragraph on the accessor surface downstream tools read.

Validation record

  • inst/validation/benchmark_scaling.{md,csv} carry the 2026-08-22 ceilings study on a realistic multi-term MET design. The flexyBayes/INLA ceiling on that design family is bracketed between 911,808 rows (the preflight refuses) and 1,823,616 rows (the engine dies after 41.6 minutes) and has not been measured or bisected. A previously recorded 340.9-second success at 911,808 rows was found unsupported by any run artefact and was corrected.
  • The execution grid gains cells for the space-level factor, Gaussian weights on both engines, and the per-trial field.
  • cran-comments.md names the check artefacts this release produces and states the dormant log-posterior contract’s oracle gap.

flexyBayes 0.9.2

Bug fixes

  • The prior mini-language refuses malformed specifications instead of substituting a default. fb_prior() matched a distribution call against the family’s parameter list and, when the match failed (as it does for a wrong argument name), carried the call on unnamed. Every emit-side read then fell back to its own default. half_normal(sd = 1.5) fitted under half_normal(scale = 1), pc(upper = 1) fitted under a tail probability the caller never wrote, and a negative standard deviation reached the sampler and surfaced four layers downstream as a missing-draws error. Argument matching is strict: an unknown or duplicated argument name, a missing required argument, a non-scalar or non-finite value, and a value outside its domain are each refused at construction with a flexybayes_refusal_* class, and both halves of a PC prior are required. The whole constructor surface is typed, so a caller can match a refusal by class instead of by message text.

  • Gamma and beta fit on the Stan backend again, on every prior route. Which families carry a residual sigma was written down twice, and the two lists disagreed: the prior emit believed gamma and beta had one, the heteroscedastic-residual gate knew they did not. The prior emit won, so every route, including the plain default with no prior argument, sent brms a sigma prior for a parameter the model does not have, and brms refused the fit. Two of the six advertised response families were unreachable on that backend. The fact now has one table (R/family_traits.R), both call sites read it, a test grounds it against brms’s own declaration of each family’s distributional parameters, and a second test fails if a duplicate roster reappears.

  • prior_fixed_sd and prior_vc_sd reach the engine, and prior_summary() tells one story about them. Both arguments were documented as applied and neither was. prior_fixed_sd was absent from the condition that decides whether the auto-default prior fires, so passing it alone left the default in charge and the legacy bridge (the only consumer of the scalar) was never reached.
